rows.src: The National Archives, Kew — Discovery, the whole catalogue
rows.what: The name in nine spellings, the Cardiff thread, and the ship — the first time this archive has ever asked Kew anything
rows.got:
**Seven records of the name in Britain, 1677 to 1934, and none of them was in this archive before.** Discovery is free, needs no key, and answers JSON at `discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/API/search/records?sps.searchQuery=` — David found it; this archive had not looked at Kew once in its life.

· **SP 99/53/290**, 18/28 November 1677 — *«Franceschi to Gio. della Torre and reply»*, in the State Papers for **Venice**.
· **HCA 45/48/2**, 1805 — a prize appeal from the Vice-Admiralty Court of **Minorca**; the captured ship *Amabile*, **master Mark Franceschi**.
· **WO 372/7/142208–142210**, 1914–1920 — three Great War medal cards, catalogued consecutively: **Lorenzo** (Dorsetshire Regiment, Private 20943), **Ernest** (Middlesex Regiment, Private G/57727), **William C.** (Royal Field Artillery, Driver 69431).
· **HO 334/134/4102** and **HO 144/19309**, 1934 — **Lorenzo Franceschi**, from Italy, resident in London, wife **Agnes Elizabeth**, certificate **AZ4102** issued 4 April 1934. The certificate and the Home Office file, for one man.

**A Lorenzo on a 1914–18 medal card and a Lorenzo naturalising out of Italy in London in 1934 may well be one man** — served first, naturalised after. *(inf — two references, not yet joined.)*

**The sweep behind that.** *«Defranceschi»* 0 · *«Defranceski»* 0 · *«De Franceski»* 0 · *«Franceski»* 0 · *«De Francheschi»* 0 · *«De Franceschi»* 3 · *«Dei Franceschi»* 4 · *Franceschi* 19 · *Francesch\** 42 · *Defrance\** 7. Eleven further records are **Franceschin-**, the diminutive and a different surname, filed as adjacent rather than as this name; three are Piero della Francesca, catalogued as *«Piero dei Franceschi»*.

**The Cardiff thread drew a blank in every direction.** *«Emerico De Franceschi»* 0 · *«De Franceschi» AND Cardiff* 0 · *Bujanovich* 0 · *Lacovich* 0 · *Cattarinich* 0 · *Lussinpiccolo* 0.

**And the ship is the lesson.** *Aquilone* returns **501 records and every one is an Admiralty muster for HMS Aquilon**, a Royal Navy ship of the line. The Cardiff barque of December 1877 is not among them.

**The first reading of that was wrong and is retracted before it was ever published.** This log was about to say that merchant shipping is catalogued by ship and year rather than by master. **It is not**: the crew lists in **BT 99** and **BT 400** are catalogued to the individual, and a title from them reads *«Ship: Belgravian; Official number: 98611. William G S Nash; rank/rating, Master; age, 57; place…»* — name, rank, age and place of birth. So a master of this name **would** be findable — and **tested directly, he is not there**. *Franceschi rank rating* **0** · *Defranceschi seaman* **0**, against **827** for *«place of birth, Italy» master*, which shows the index is dense rather than thin. The person-level cataloguing reaches back well before 1915: **BT 99/1302/37 is 1881** and **BT 99/1718/16B is 1891**, both giving name, rating, age and birthplace. The right question is therefore not whether the index reaches people but **whether Kew's sample covers Cardiff in 1876–77**, because most nineteenth-century crew agreements went to Newfoundland and Kew keeps a fraction. **A negative here is a negative in the index, not at Kew**, and the index is better than it first looked. [Britain, on the map of the name](/diaspora/#britain).

rows.src: Archivinformationssystem — the whole Austrian State Archives, searched by name for the first time
rows.what: Whether the ÖStA catalogue names this family — and whether the €45 the Kriegsarchiv quoted would buy anything
rows.got:
**Ninety-nine records, fifty-three of them the name, and the Kriegsarchiv's own bill is answered by its own catalogue.**

The Austrian State Archives publish a field search that is free, needs no account, and searches **Title contains** across every department. Nobody here had ever run it. One query on the stem *Franceschi* returns **99 records: 53 of this name, 46 of the adjacent diminutives** — AVA 19, FHKA 12, HHStA 11, Kriegsarchiv 7, AdR 4.

**The €45 question is settled, and the answer is half a refund.** On 17 September the Kriegsarchiv quoted €45, payable win or lose, for a *Marinepersonensuche* on Julius and Valentin.

· **Valentin needs no search at all.** He is catalogued to the item: **AT-OeStA/KA Marine NMA PA Offiziere und Beamte Akten QL 944 — DEFRANCESCHI, Valentin, Administrations-Assistent**, a naval *Qualifikationsliste*. *«Permission required: Keine · Accessibility: Öffentlich.»* A file you can cite is a **reproduction order**, not a research fee.

· **Julius is not in the catalogue at all** — and the Kriegsarchiv's own FAQ says why: personnel records of navy men **born after 1865** whose *Heimatzuständigkeit* lay outside today's Austria *«verblieben in den jeweiligen Nachfolgestaaten bzw. wurden dorthin abgetreten»*. Julius was born 1879 on the Kvarner. **His file went to Yugoslavia in 1918.** Vienna quoted to look for something its own website says it does not hold.

**Three men of the name this archive had never met.**

· **Johann Defranceschi, born 1833, Geburtsort Gallignana — which is Gračišće**, the parish this family comes out of. A sailor: *Marinediener 4. Klasse* on one card and *1. Klasse* on two others, so the promotion is visible in the catalogue alone. Three files: **MGBBl 2651**, **VerEv Kdi 219**, **VerEv KL-Mardi 76**.

· **Carl «Dragutin» Defranceschi, born 29 July 1883 at Zara, judge at the district court of Šibenik** — personnel file 1909–1918, **AVA Justiz JM Präs. A 134.22**. An Italian and a Croatian forename on one man in one file, which is this archive's whole thesis in miniature.

· **Peter Defranceschi, Ordensverleihung 1918** — **Ritterkreuz, Kriegsdekoration mit Schwert**, HHStA HA OrdK Kartei **3-168**, Geschäftszahl **1732/1918**. The card only; the act itself sits under the Ordenskanzlei files for 1918.

**And a family of Habsburg accountants nobody had counted.** The Hofkammerarchiv holds **Vicenzo** (Kassa 46, 1847), **Anton** (ORH 3412, *Dalmatinische Provinzial-Staatsbuchhaltung in Zara*), **Johann Baptist** and a second **Valentin** (ORH 3777 and 3778, both *Zentralstaatsbuchhaltung in Venedig*). Venice and Zadar, the two ends of the Adriatic, in one office.

*Method, so it can be repeated: `archivinformationssystem.at/feldsuche.aspx` → row 1 «Title» / «contains» / term; set results per page; Search. Searching the stem **Franceschi** catches every in-scope spelling and the diminutives in one pass.*

---

**Superseded, 22 September 2026.** This row says **four** accountants. **There are nine**, and the Venice office alone holds five — the September search was run with the form's default operator, *«starts with»*, which drops every **De**franceschi. *The row is left as it was written, because a search register records what a search returned; the count is corrected on* [the corrections page](/corrections/) *and all nine are on the roster.*

rows.src: TNA Discovery — where the nineteenth-century crew agreements actually are
rows.what: Whether Kew or Newfoundland holds a Cardiff crew agreement for 1876–77
rows.got:
**Neither, and both, and a third — in stated proportions.** Kew's own series description for **BT 99** calls it *«a **ten per cent sample** of agreements and crew lists … for the years 1861-1938»*. Discovery separately catalogues, as an external holding, *«Registrar General of Shipping and Seamen, crew lists, agreements and official logbooks (**c70% of total**)», 1863-1938*, held by the **Maritime History Archive, Memorial University of Newfoundland**. The remaining fifth sits in **county record offices** — for a Cardiff ship, Glamorgan Archives.

**The key to all three is a number, not a name.** **MF17** at Kew is the microfiche *«Index to location of crew agreements and logbooks of vessels», 1863-1913*, produced by the Newfoundland archive itself and *«arranged according to the **official number** of the vessel, the vessels are not named»*. Every BT 99 piece in the catalogue is likewise titled by official numbers only.

**So the surname will never find a crew list, however dense the index.** The lookup runs ship → official number → MF17 → repository. That makes the **Cardiff marriage certificate of Q3 1876** the hinge: it is the one document that might name Emerico's vessel.

rows.src: Hungaricana — the given name varied sixteen ways, for the first time
rows.what: Whether the Hungarian forms of the forenames find people the German and Italian forms missed
rows.got:
**Sixteen Hungarian forenames, fourteen nils, two hits — and the two explain the fourteen.**

Every sweep this archive had run varied the **surname** and never the **forename**. So sixteen Magyar forms went to Hungaricana as phrases in Hungarian word order, surname first: *Gyula, Antal, János, Bálint, Vincze, Károly, Mihály, József, Miklós, Alajos, Tódor, Lajos, István, Ede* — **all zero**.

**«Defranceschi Ferencz» returns 4** and **«Defranceschi Péter» returns 1.** Which gives the rule: the Hungarian state wrote its *prose* in Hungarian and its *service lists* in German, so **the surname inverts but the forename stays put**. *Ferencz* works only because it is a **spelling** of Franz, not a translation of it.

**The four Ferencz hits include one that is new** — the **Budapesti utasító of 1848**, a Budapest directory, beside the two already-known pension entries for the Fiume harbour master and his orphan daughter.

**And Péter gave a man nobody here had met:** *«beim Husz. Reg. Nr 8 · **Defranceschi Peter Dr** · beim Garnisons-Spitale zu …»*, **Militärschematismus des österreichischen Kaiserthumes für 1867**, p. 647, under *Militär-Parteien*. A **regimental physician** — now the fourteenth name on [the imperial roll](/imperial/) and the second doctor on it.

*The fourteen nils are evidence rather than silence because the control worked: a method that returns four known records for Ferencz is a method whose zeros can be believed.*
ev: The Kvarner households — Rijeka and Bakar

rows.src: NSK digitalna — the National and University Library's full text, both spellings
rows.what: What Croatian digitised books and journals say about the name — the search that had stood pending for a week
rows.got:
**The name turns out to have a village it never left, and an inscription nobody here knew about.**

**Svetvinčenat — and the name is the only one that stayed.** *Atti* 48 (2018), the journal of the Centro di ricerche storiche at Rovigno: *«Il cognome **Defranceschi** era stato l'unico ad avere nel **Castello di San Vincenti** una continuità…»* — **the only surname with continuity in the castle of San Vincenti**. And it acted as a body: *«Guidati da **Antonio Defranceschi**, nel **1780** avevano ottenuto l'esonero dal partecipare alla difesa armata»* — **led by Antonio Defranceschi, in 1780 they obtained exemption from armed defence duty.** This archive had never heard of Svetvinčenat.

**A Glagolitic inscription at Gologorica.** Branko Fučić, *Glagoljski natpisi* (JAZU, Zagreb 1982) — the standard corpus — carries: *«Natpis je vjerojatno registriran u **Gologorici**, gdje su **Defranceschi**…»*. **Gologorica is one of this archive's own origin places.**

**The sentence was then walked out of the closed book a phrase at a time** — the full-text index re-centres its snippet on whatever phrase you search, so a copyright-restricted page can be read forwards in steps: *«Riječ »**Pomjane**« (ime istarskog sela) ne može se čitati u posljednjem retku. Natpis je vjerojatno registriran u Gologorici, **gdje su Defranceschi imali posjed i** …»* — *«…where the Defranceschi **had an estate and** …»*

**So it is not a mention, it is a landholding**, and Fučić uses it to date the stone. **Pomjane** — the unreadable village in the inscription's last line — is a place-name new to this archive.

**The surname survey puts the name in four more Istrian places.** *Atti* 50 (2020) lists it under **GALLIGNANA** — which is **Gračišće** — and under **VISINADA/Vižinada**, **BARBAN** and **KRŠIKLA**, together with two compound forms this archive has never recorded: **Defranceschi Triscoli** and **Defranceschi Pelosi**.

**Three more, each of a different kind.** A woman holding land: *«**Elena Defranceschi** Vittorio 669 Dobasnizza Polje»* in Carlo Hugues, *Il carbonato calcico* (Parenzo 1896), a register of Istrian vineyard plots. A political line-up: *«**FACHINETTI — MADONIZZA - DEFRANCESCHI**»* in Pacifico Valussi, *Trieste e l'Istria* (Milano **1861**) — the name set beside the two best-known Istrian liberals of the year. And a citation: *«Fra i moderni citiamo **Carlo Defranceschi: «L'Istria», note storiche, Parenzo**»*, G. E. Pons, *Antichità polesi* (Pola 1910).

**And the spaced spelling opens the scholarship.** 43 records against 10. *Vjesnik Istarskog arhiva* 25 (2018) carries Jurković's bibliography of the journal's first twenty-five volumes, and it indexes **four authors of the name: DE FRANCESCHI, Camillo · Carlo · **Ettore** · **Paolo***. **Ettore and Paolo are new here.** The same volume cites *Camillo DE FRANCESCHI, Storia documentata della Contea di Pisino, a cura del figlio* — edited by his son, which names a generation.

*Method: `digitalna.nsk.hr`, «Cjeloviti tekst» box. The old `dnc.nsk.hr` portal is a dead shell and should not be cited again.*

rows.src: JUSP Jasenovac — the named victims list, on the surname and on both her married names
rows.what: Whether Anka Nera, or anyone of the name, is among the named victims of the Jasenovac camps
rows.got:
**Nobody of this name is in it, in any spelling — and Anka is not in it under either married name.**

The Jasenovac Memorial Site publishes its *Poimenični popis žrtava*, the named list of victims of the Jasenovac and Stara Gradiška camps, searchable free by surname. **Defranceschi: 0. Defranceski: 0. Franceschi: 0.**

**The control was run first**, because a nil from a search box proves nothing until the box is known to answer: *Horvat* returns pages of results, with father's name, birth year, birthplace and nationality on each row. So the zeros are evidence.

**Her married name returns four people and none of them is her.** *Oreščanin* gives **Đuro** (b. 1894, Karlovac), **Jelena** (b. 1878, Inđija), **Ljubomir** (b. 1906, Zagreb) and **Ranko** (b. 1894, Inđija) — all recorded as Serbs, none a woman born at Crikvenica in 1915. *Geiger* gives two, **Đeno-Jeno** (b. 1884, Subotica) and **Julio** (b. 1913, Zagreb), both recorded as Jews and neither her first husband — who died in **1936**, before any of this.

**What the second negative is worth.** Arolsen already said she died outside the **German** system. Jasenovac now says she died outside the **Ustaša camp** system too. A Croatian woman of twenty-nine dead in **Belgrade in 1944** is therefore not a camp death that the family softened into a city name — **she died in the city, and the records that would say how are Serbian, not Croatian and not German**.

*And the nil has a second use: it is the first time the whole surname has been put to a victims list. For a study of the name rather than of one family, «nobody of this name is in Jasenovac» is a finding in its own right.*

rows.src: Crikvenica marriages 1895 — Petar Kovačina, joiner, and the resort being built
rows.what: Reading the marriage film for Defranceschi turned up the other side of the family instead
rows.got:
**The film was being read for a name that is not in it, and gave a different one that is.**

**Crikvenica marriages 1895, entry 28, 28 November: «Petar Kovačina, stolar» — a joiner — marries «Marija Car», at Crikvenica house 119.** Both are entered as workers; his father is another **Petar Kovačina**.

**Kovačina is Uršula's surname.** **Uršula Kovačina**, born at Crikvenica about 1890–95, married **Anton Rudolf Defranceschi** and is David's great-grandmother — she is on [the direct line](/direct-line/) and died at Belgrade in 1975. A **Kovačina household at Crikvenica in 1895, in the joiner's trade, with a house number**, is the first time this archive has seen her family in a register rather than in a tree. *inf — kinship is not yet proved; a Kovačina at Crikvenica in 1895 is very likely her kin, but which kin is a question for the birth register.*

**What settles it:** the **Crikvenica births for 1890–1896**, which are on [the errands](/errands/) already for a different reason, would show whether Uršula is a daughter of this house.

**And the page it sits on is worth reading for its own sake.** The same three images carry **Josip Butković, deputy manager of the Grande Hotel**; two carpenters named **Stumpfhuber**; **Alojzije Jerkini, architect and clerk of works**; labourers from **Ljubljana**; a clerk from **Karlovac-Dubovac** with a **Herbst** witness; and a **post-and-telegraph official from Gospić** married with a **plemeniti Budisavljević** standing witness. **Crikvenica's Grand Hotel was going up, and the register is full of the people building and running it.** That is the world an Italian-named craftsman would have belonged to — and the name is still not there.

rows.src: Crikvenica marriages 1899 — a Kalanj in the book, and he is not Anna's brother
rows.what: The second surname of the Klenovica marriage finally appears in the Crikvenica register
rows.got:
**Crikvenica marriages, 1899, entry 1, 8 January: «Ivan Kalanj, zidar» — a mason — marries «Vjekoslava Car, poljodjelka».** His parents are **Ivan Kalanj and Josipa née Šilić**, labourers; hers are Jakov Car, a sailor, and Marija née Kalnić.

**Kalanj is the surname this archive has been hunting alongside Defranceschi.** **Anna Kalanj** married **Josip Defranceschi** and is Anton Rudolf's mother; the marriage this whole film was opened to find is *theirs*. So a Kalanj in the Crikvenica book matters.

**And the parents rule him out as her brother, which is worth saying plainly.** Anna Kalanj was baptised at **Ledenice in 1864**, «daughter of **Josephus Kalanj and Rosalia née Perković**, at Klenovica house 22». This groom's parents are **Ivan and Josipa née Šilić**. **Different household.** He is not her brother, and nothing here connects him to her beyond the surname.

*What it does establish* is that **Kalanj was present at Crikvenica** and marrying there — the name is in the parish, in the building trades, in 1899. That is a place to look for Anna's kin that this archive did not have, and it sharpens the question the film was opened to answer: **the Kalanj were reachable from Crikvenica, and the Defranceschi still are not in it.**

rows.src: Crikvenica marriages 1899 — Anna Kalanj's brother, found by reading the film that does not contain her husband
rows.what: Whether any Kalanj of Anna's own household appears in the Crikvenica register
rows.got:
**Crikvenica marriages, 1899, entry 12, 25 January:**

> *«**Josip Kalanj, zidar**, iz **Ledenica**» — a mason, of **Ledenice house 37** — marries *«**Marija Poštrenčić, švelja**»*, a seamstress, now living at Crikvenica. His parents: **«Josip Kalanj i Rosalija rodj. Perković»**. A witness: **«Luka Kalanj Martinov, zidar»**.

**Those are Anna Kalanj's parents.** This archive already held her baptism: **Ledenice, 1864, «entry 2, daughter of Josephus Kalanj and Rosalia née Perković, at Klenovica house 22»**. Same father's name, same mother, same maiden name, same parish. **Josip Kalanj the younger is Anna's brother** — and therefore **Anton Rudolf's maternal uncle** and David's great-great-uncle.

**Why it matters more than one name.** Anna Kalanj married **Josip Defranceschi**, and this whole film was opened to find *that* marriage. The film does not contain it. But it does contain **her brother**, with a **trade**, a **house number** and a **wife** — so the bride's family is now in a register rather than on a chart, and **the Kalanj turn out to be masons**, the same building trade that fills these pages while Crikvenica's hotel was going up.

**The house number differs and that is expected**: Anna is at **Klenovica 22** in 1864, her brother at **Ledenice 37** in 1899. Klenovica is a hamlet of Ledenice and thirty-five years separate the two entries.

**And a second Kalanj stands beside him** — *Luka Kalanj, son of Martin, mason*. A third, **Ivan Kalanj**, married in this same register three weeks earlier (1899 no. 1) to different parents. **There is a Kalanj colony of masons working between Ledenice and Crikvenica in 1899.**

*doc — the parents' names are read directly off the page; the maiden name «Perković» is a handwriting read, checked at full magnification.*

**What to do next:** the **Ledenice marriage register** should hold Josip and Marija's banns, and the **Ledenice births around 1860–1875** should hold Anna and her brothers together in one household — which would give this archive **Anna's whole sibling set** for the first time.

rows.src: Novi Vinodolski — the parish that serves Klenovica, checked at the source
rows.what: Whether the marriage of Josip Defranceschi and Anna Kalanj can be found at Novi Vinodolski, the parish named as the next place to look when the Crikvenica film came up empty
rows.got:
**It cannot, and the reason is worth writing down rather than repeating the guess.**

**Novi Vinodolski has no marriage register on film after 1859.** Queried directly against the FamilySearch waypoint tree rather than against this archive's own harvested copy: the parish has **seven** filmed volumes, and its only marriage books are **Vjenčani 1674–1786** and **Vjenčani 1787–1859**. The rest are baptisms (1650–1784, 1784–1804, 1804–1852, 1852–1874, **1875–1900**) and deaths (1784–1823, 1823–1859, 1859–1888, 1888–1899). *There is no volume in which this marriage could be.*

**And Anton Rudolf is not in Novi's baptism book either — which is the part that actually teaches something.** He was born at **Klenovica house 22 on 20 January 1890, baptised 9 February**, and Klenovica sits in the Novi Vinodolski municipality, so the 1875–1900 baptism volume was the obvious place. It was opened and the entries around that date were read: **image 249 closes 1889 and opens 1890 at entries 1–4** (1, 4, 12 and 4 January); **image 250 runs entries 5–11**, 14 January to 6 April; **image 251 runs 12–19**, to late June. **No Defranceschi anywhere in them.**

**Because Klenovica had its own church.** This archive's own plate of the baptism says so in the priest's words — *«u ovoj župnoj crkvi»*, in **this** parish church — and the register it comes from is catalogued not under Novi but as **«Matične knjige, Ledenice / Klenovica»**. **Klenovica does not exist as a parish in the FamilySearch tree at all**, so its books are not filmed and cannot be read this way.

**One line of that entry redirects the whole search.** The remarks column explains why the birth happened at Klenovica at all: *«Roditelji djeteta nahodeć se kod svojih u Klenovici, t.j. kod roditelja žene Ane, dobiše ovo djete»* — **the parents, being with their own people at Klenovica, that is with the parents of the wife Ana, had this child.** So in January 1890 the couple **did not live at Klenovica**. They were visiting. **Klenovica is Ana's parents' house, not theirs** — which is consistent with the godfather being **Jakov Kalanj of that same house 22**.

*nil — the register that would answer the question is not on film; the register that was on film has been read and does not contain them.*

rows.src: Sv. Jakov-Šiljevica marriages 1882–1891 — read end to end
rows.what: Whether Josip Defranceschi and Anna Kalanj married in the small Vinodol parish next to Klenovica, whose marriage film — contrary to this archive's earlier survey — does cover the years wanted
rows.got:
**Ten years read, both surnames visible on every line, and the name is not there.**

The volume is **Vjenčani 1859–1910**, eighty-three images for fifty-one years — a parish of six to ten marriages a year. Its left page carries **both spouses with their condition, the origin and domicile of each, religion, age and status**, so a single crop of the left page shows every surname and every place in the entry.

**Images 35 to 46 were read: 1882 from entry 5, then 1883, 1884, 1885, 1886, 1887, 1888, 1889, 1890 and 1891 complete.** That covers the whole window in which this marriage can fall — Ana Kalanj was born in January 1864 and her first known child in January 1890.

**Year totals, off the priest's own numbering:** 1882 closes at 10, 1883 at 5, 1884 at 8, 1885 at 6, 1886 at 10, 1887 at 7, 1888 at 7, 1889 at 4, 1890 at 6 or more, 1891 at 5 or more. **About seventy marriages, and not one Defranceschi.**

**It is a closed parish of eight surnames.** *Grbić/Grbčić, Abel, Crhak, Šegulja, Turčić, Pavlić, Damian, Šepac, Malčić, Perhat, Knez, Blažić, Mlanfar* — marrying each other between **Klošter, Šiljevica, Smokovo, Katun, Sv. Jakov** and **Mlanfari**. **Klenovica never appears in the origin column at all**, which is itself an answer: this parish did not serve it.

**Two outsiders in ten years, and the register named both in full** — **Mate Piškulić, kr. financijski čuvar**, a royal finance guard of Novi marrying a Trsat woman domiciled at Kraljevica (1882 no. 10), and **a miller with an Italian surname from «Piran — Istrija»** marrying a Turčić (1890 no. 6). *The same test as at Crikvenica: when a stranger married here the clerk wrote down his trade and his birthplace. Ours never had to be written.*

*nil — ten complete years, left page of every spread, both surname columns.*

rows.src: A catalogue correction: two Vinodol parishes DO have marriage films covering 1883–1889
rows.dest: Vinodol — Bribir, Sv. Jakov-Šiljevica, Ledenice, Novi Vinodolski
rows.what: Re-checking the shelf survey that sent this archive to Crikvenica, against the live FamilySearch waypoint tree rather than a harvested copy
rows.got:
**The survey that opened the Crikvenica film said that across the whole Vinodol only one marriage register on film reached the 1880s. That was wrong by two parishes.**

Queried parish by parish on 20 September 2026:

| parish | marriage volumes on film | covers 1883–89? |
|---|---|---|
| **Crikvenica** | 1800–1858 · **1859–1908** | yes — **read, negative** |
| **Bribir** | 1678–1738 · 1815–1821, 1853–1858 · **1858–1900** | **yes — not yet read** |
| **Sv. Jakov-Šiljevica** | 1821–1859 · **1859–1910** | **yes — read, negative** |
| Ledenice | 1734–1825 · 1826–1865 · 1866–**1882** | no |
| Novi Vinodolski | 1674–1786 · 1787–**1859** | no |
| Grižane | 1735–1858 only | no |

**So the field was never as narrow as the earlier note claimed.** Sv. Jakov-Šiljevica has now been read and is clean. **Bribir, Vjenčani 1858–1900, remains unread and is the last filmed Vinodol marriage register that could hold this marriage.**

*correction — recorded against this archive's own earlier statement, not against anybody else's.*

rows.src: Bribir marriages 1882–1890 — the last filmed Vinodol marriage register, read end to end
rows.what: The final filmed candidate for the marriage of Josip Defranceschi and Anna Kalanj — nine consecutive years covering the whole window in which it must fall
rows.got:
**Nine years, close to four hundred marriages, both surnames legible on every line, and the name is not there.**

**First, a trap in the catalogue worth recording.** The waypoint for *Vjenčani 1858–1900* returns **597 images**, because Bribir's births, marriages and deaths share one reel and the catalogue gives them the same film ark. Probing found deaths at images 300, 420, 480 and 540 and **the marriages around image 120**. The marriage section runs roughly **images 108–150**; everything from about 250 onward is the death register.

**Year by year, off the priest's own numbering:**

| year | marriages | pages |
|---|---|---|
| 1883 | **57** | 102–106 |
| 1884 | **45** | 107–109 |
| 1885 | **64** | 110–113 |
| 1886 | **41** | 114–116 |
| 1887 | **45** | 117–120 |
| 1888 | **25** | 121–125 |
| 1889 | **22** | 126–129 |
| 1890 | **24** | 130–132 |

With the tail of 1882 that is **about four hundred marriages read**, and **no Defranceschi in any of them.**

**Bribir is the biggest of these parishes and the most closed.** Sixty-four marriages in 1885, most of them crammed into the three weeks before Lent — twelve on 11 January alone. And they are the same thirty surnames over and over: **Antonić, Krsul, Krajačić, Kalafatić, Dražić, Simac, Špoja, Tonković, Skvirić, Juden, Kombol, Stanić, Čor, Ugrin, Pipinić, Škočilić, Marinčić, Pohmajević** — marrying each other between **Štale, Podgori, Kričina, Sv. Vid, Sv. Mikula, Kosavin, Jargovo, Dragaljin, Gradac, Podskoči, Ugrin** and **Podugrinac**.

**The outsiders are countable and the register named every one.** *Paskval Freca «iz Rieke, u Bribiru nastanjen»* and *Fran Bontić of Rijeka* (1883); *Lovre Krmpotić of **Ledenice*** (1885); a bride from **Novi** (1886); *Mate Barac of **Grižane*** (1888); **Luka Roman Josip Vrinjanin, merchant, of Krasica donja, domiciled at Crikvenica** (1889); *Stanko Belošević, joiner, of Petrovsko near Krapina* (1889). And the best of them, **1888 no. 22: «G. Ulrich Hofer, mjestni učitelj pučke učione» of Karlovac marrying «Teresia Antolić, učiteljica ovdašnje pučke učione» of Zagreb** — the village schoolmaster and schoolmistress marrying each other, both written down with their posts.

**Method note, because the film fought back.** The reel photographs the whole spread in one frame with wide black margins, so the Crikvenica crop did not fit; the working left-page window is `x 0.085 w 0.300, y 0.055 h 0.855`. An early crop at `h 0.64` clipped the last two or three entries of each page — **the gaps that created (p.104 nos 35–36 and p.105 no. 48) were gone back for and filled**, so the run is continuous. The reel also carries **duplicate frames** (images 114 and 115 are the same page), so pages, not images, are the unit that matters.

*nil — 1882 in part, then 1883 to 1890 complete, left page of every spread, no gaps.*

rows.src: Anna Kalanj's whole household, and the house she was born in
rows.what: The sibling set of Anna Kalanj, and whether the Kalanj house at Klenovica can be tied to the house in her own baptism
rows.got:
**Eight children, and the same front door for thirty years.**

The **Ledenice baptism register 1861–1894** gives the children of **Josip Kalanj and Rosalija née Perković** — David's great-great-grandparents on the Kvarner side. Found through the FamilySearch index on `q.fatherSurname=Kalanj`, then **every one of them read back on the register page itself**:

| child | born | baptised | house as the clerk wrote it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Thomas** | 1858 | — | *(earlier volume, not yet read on the page)* |
| **Martinus** | 10 Nov 1861 | — | **«Ledenice in Klenovica N° 22»** |
| **ANNA** | **3 Jan 1864** | **6 Jan** | **«Rljinovica N° 22»** |
| **Lucia** | 24 May 1866 | — | **«Ledenice N° 22, in Rljenovice»** |
| **Franciscus** | 30 Sep 1868 | — | *(parents verified; locus not yet read)* |
| **Josephus** | **5 May 1871** | **7 May** | **«Povile N° 22»** |
| **Maria** | 19 Mar 1874 | — | *(parents verified; locus not yet read)* |
| **Joannes** | 18/20 Jul 1877 | — | **«Povile N° 2…»** |

**Anna's own entry, page 24, entry 2, read at full magnification:** born **3 January 1864**, baptised **6 January**, *legitima*, of **«Josephus Kalanj … et Rosalia nata Perković ejus uxor, ruricolae»**, at **Rljinovica N° 22**, godparents **Josephus Ban and his wife Anna**, baptised by **Vincentius Šegulja, parochus administrator**. *This also reconciles two dates that looked like a contradiction: the archive had 3 January, the index says 6 January. They are the birth and the baptism, and both are right.*

## The house

**The clerk names one house four ways across sixteen years — Klenovica, Rljinovica, Rljenovice, Povile — and the number never changes. It is always 22.** In 1861 he writes it out in full: **«Ledenice in Klenovica N° 22»**.

**And Anton Rudolf Defranceschi was born at «Klenovica kbr. 22» on 20 January 1890.**

So **Anna Kalanj was born in the same house as her son**, twenty-six years apart, and the 1890 baptism's remark — *«kod roditelja žene Ane»*, with the wife Ana's parents — is naming **this** household. The godfather of 1890, **Jakov Kalanj of house 22**, belongs to it too.

*One honest caveat.* Klenovica, Klenovica and Povile are three named places on and above that stretch of coast. The 1861 entry ties **Klenovica** and **22** to these exact parents, and 1864 and 1866 tie **Klenovica** and **22** to them; **Povile 22** in 1871 and 1877 may be the same house under a neighbouring hamlet's name or a short move along the shore. **The number, the parish and the parents are firm; which of the three names the building itself stood under is not settled by these entries alone.**

## What it gives the archive

**Anna Kalanj stops being a name on a chart.** She is the **third of eight**, with an elder brother Thomas and Martinus above her and five below — and the youngest of them, **Josephus, born 5 May 1871**, is exactly the **«Josip Kalanj, zidar, of Ledenice house 37»** who married Marija Poštrenčić at Crikvenica in January 1899 and was identified as her brother from that entry's parents. **The two findings now confirm each other from opposite ends.**

*doc — index used only to locate the pages; every date and every house number above that is not marked otherwise was read off the register image.*

rows.src: The index, asked straight out for a Defranceschi married to a Kalanj
rows.what: Whether the marriage of Josip Defranceschi and Anna Kalanj is anywhere in the FamilySearch index, in any parish in Croatia
rows.got:
**It is not, and the question had never been put this way.**

Two queries against the Croatia Church Books index, on the fields that actually work: **`q.spouseSurname=Kalanj`** across Croatia, and **`q.surname=Defranceschi / Defranceski / Franceschi`** across Croatia. Six hundred rows came back for the surname and a hundred for the Kalanj spouse.

**Every «Franc-» name among the Kalanj marriages is a forename or a different surname** — *Franciscus, Francisca, Franković, Frković*. **There is no marriage of a Defranceschi to a Kalanj in the index at all.**

*That is the expected answer and it is worth having explicitly.* The index only knows what has been filmed, and the register this marriage should be in — **Klenovica, or Ledenice after 1882** — is not filmed. **A negative from the index is not a negative from the record.**

rows.src: The surname put straight to the index — and two children's entries read back
rows.what: What the FamilySearch index holds for the name in the Vinodol, checked row by row against the register images
rows.got:
**Six hundred indexed rows for the name in Croatia; fifteen touch the Vinodol; two of them matter, and they pull in opposite directions.**

**1. A correction. «Marija Stjepanka Defranceschi, 22 Dec 1892, Ledenice».** This archive had her as *born 8 December 1892 at Crikvenica*. The page — **Ledenice baptisms p.166 no. 83** — says born **8 December**, baptised **22 December**, at **Ledenice**, of **«Josip Defranceschi, klesar, i žena Ana Kalanj rodjena»**, residence **«Klenovica kbroj 28, na stan»** — Klenovica house 28, **in lodgings**. *So the family were still in the Ledenice parish at the end of 1892, living in rented rooms a few doors from Ana's parents at house 22.* Logged as [a correction](/corrections/).

**2. A confirmation, and the index is the one that is wrong.** The index gives *«Zorica De Franceski, Jul 1897, Crikvenica»*; this archive has her born **14 December 1896**. The page — **Crikvenica baptisms p.299 no. 143** — says born **14 December 1896**, baptised **17 January 1897**. **The archive's date is right and the index garbled it.** The entry is worth having for its own sake: the father is written **«Josip Defranceschi Antonov iz Gračišća, klesar u mjestu»** — *son of Anton, of Gračišće, stonecutter in this place*. **The Istrian origin and the patronymic are written into a Kvarner register in the priest's own hand.**

*The lesson is the one this archive keeps relearning: the index is a finding aid and nothing more. Both rows had to be read on the page, and one of them was wrong.*

rows.src: The Kovačina marriage of 1895 — and the question the archive refused to guess at
rows.what: Whether Petar Kovačina the joiner of house 119 was the financial guard under an earlier trade, a brother, or a son
rows.got:
**He is the son, and the marriage entry says so in as many words.**

This archive set the question out honestly and declined to answer it: two Crikvenica death entries gave a **Petar Kovačina, «umirovljeni c. kr. financijski Nadstražar»**, who died on 3 November 1904 aged 55 with his wife **Uršula née Stojčić**, and a **Petar Kovačina, «stolar»**, a joiner, married to **Marija née Car** — *both at house 119*. *«Whether the joiner is the guard under an earlier trade, a brother, or a son, the register does not say and this archive will not guess.»*

**The marriage register does say.** Crikvenica marriages, **28 November 1895**, entry 28 — read on the film, and the parents' cell magnified to be certain of it:

> **«Petar Kovačina, stolar»** marries **«Marija Car»** at **Crikvenica house 119**.
> **Parents of the groom: «Petar Kovačina, k. r. financ. nadstražar, i Uršula rodj. Stojčić, radnica.»**
> Parents of the bride: **«Vjekoslav Car i [Krista?] rodj. Car»** — *the mother’s forename reads as **Krista** on the page and is indexed as **Vinka**; the surname and the father are not in doubt, the forename is.*

**Those are exactly the two people from the 1904 death entry** — the same name, the same office in the same words, the same wife with the same maiden name. **The joiner is the guard's son.**

**So the house resolves into three generations:**

1. **Petar Kovačina the elder** — *c. kr. financijski nadstražar*, a senior guard of the Habsburg customs and excise, born at **Draga in the kotar of Sušak** about 1849, dead of consumption at Crikvenica on **3 November 1904**; and **Uršula «Ursa» née Stojčić**, *kućarka*.
2. **Petar Kovačina the younger** — **stolar**, a joiner — who married **Marija Car** on **28 November 1895** and kept house 119. The observations add why the wedding needed paperwork: *«dozvolom kr. ug. Ministarstva za zem. obranu od 14/9 t.g. br. 53688»* — **by leave of the Royal Hungarian Ministry of National Defence**, so he was still of service age. Their daughter **Josipa** died there at eighteen months in September 1898.
3. **Uršula Kovačina**, who married **Anton Rudolf Defranceschi** — *and who carries her grandmother's name*.

**One step is inference and is flagged as such.** That Anton Rudolf's wife Uršula is the daughter of the joiner and Marija Car is the natural reading — the name, the house and the dates all fit a girl born at 119 in the later 1890s — **but it is not yet proved**. The proof would be her own baptism: **Crikvenica births, 1896–1902, a Uršula Kovačina at house 119.** That is the next thing to read.

*doc for the three named generations; the link from the joiner to Anton Rudolf's wife is inf until that baptism is found.*

**And the next step was tried at once: it does not answer.** The index was queried for every child of a Kovačina father in Croatia — four hundred rows — and **there is no Uršula Kovačina birth in it at all**. Either her baptism is unindexed or she was born outside these books. *So the link from the joiner to Anton Rudolf’s wife stays exactly where it was: the natural reading, not yet the proved one.* Reading Crikvenica births 1896–1902 page by page is the way to settle it.

rows.src: The FamilySearch index, matched on Valentino and Helena as parents rather than on the children's names
rows.dest: Fiume — St Vitus baptisms and burials
rows.what: An ark and an image for each of Valentino's Fiume children, so the pages stop resting on an unciteable reading
rows.got:
**Eleven of fifteen recovered, a fifteenth child found, and the four that resist are exactly the four the archive had already named as unindexed.**

The children were read off the register on 6 September 2026 and **no ark or image was kept** — this archive's own rule is that a read is worth what its citation is worth, so the whole list was uncitable. Searching the index for the children's names fails, because the names are latinised differently in every entry. **Searching the surname and then filtering on date works**: `q.surname` over *Defranceschi*, *De Franceschi* and *Franceschi*, keeping only rows whose principal carries a year between **1735 and 1760**. Twenty-two rows come back for those twenty-five years; eleven of them are Valentino's.

| child | date | image | index entry |
|---|---|---|---|
| Josepha Catharina | 26 Nov 1737 | `3:1:3QS7-L99F-W4KP` | `1:2:HCZ8-L1M7` |
| Matheus Franciscus | 17 Sep 1739 | `3:1:3QS7-L99F-W4RZ` | `1:2:HCZ8-G8B7` |
| Nicolaus Francus | 4 Sep 1741 | `3:1:3QS7-899F-WH3Q` | `1:2:HCZ8-2Y4W` |
| Mattio *(burial)* | 11 Jul 1742 | `3:1:3QS7-L99F-QDHV` | `1:2:H4RW-B5PB` |
| Nicolo *(burial)* | 1742 | `3:1:3QS7-L99F-QDHV` | `1:2:H4R4-95G8` |
| Francisca Joanna Theresia | 19 Dec 1742 | `3:1:3QS7-899F-W4R7` | `1:2:HCZ8-2NF6` |
| Aloysius Joannes Petrus | 26 Jun 1752 | `3:1:3QSQ-G99F-W4VZ` | `1:2:HCZ8-K6P7` |
| Antonio *(burial)* | 1 Sep 1753 | `3:1:3QS7-899F-QDL6`​ | `1:2:H4R4-SVW9` |
| **Jacobus Vincentius** | **21 Jul 1757** | `3:1:3QS7-L99F-WWGH` | `1:2:HCZ8-24VR` |
| Aloysia *(burial)* | Sep 1757 | `3:1:3QS7-L99F-QD3H` | `1:2:H4R4-9C35` |
| Maria *(burial)* | 1757 | `3:1:3QS7-899F-QDGG` | `1:2:H4R4-9C9L` |

**Three things fall out of the table.**

**The ark prefixes are a map of the books.** `…-W…` frames are the **baptisms**, `…-QD…` frames the **burials**. That is what first suggested Aloysia's 1757 date was a death rather than a birth — and reading the page proved it, and gave her age as four.

**Mattio and Nicolo share a frame.** Both burials of 1742 sit on `3:1:3QS7-L99F-QDHV`, which is what one expects of two deaths a few entries apart in the same book — and is worth a glance on the page when someone next has it open.

**The four that never come back are the four the archive already knew about.** *Ignatius Francus Mattheus 1745, Vitus Joannes Baptista 1751, Aloysius Rochus 1754, Rosalia Francisca 1755* — named as unindexed on 6 September, before any of this was tried. **Everything the September reading recorded that could be checked has checked out**, which is the best evidence available that the four uncheckable ones were read correctly too.

*doc for the eleven; the four remaining rest on the 6 September reading alone and need the film at their dates.*

rows.src: Fiume baptisms, the page under «Die 21 July 1757»
rows.what: Whether the index's «Jacobum Vincentium» of Valentinus and Helena is really a child of this household
rows.got:
**He is, and the entry is unambiguous.**

The first crop of the frame landed on the **20 July** heading and showed *«Margaritam Annam … jugalium Danesich»* — not a Defranceschi — which briefly looked like the index pointing at the wrong page. It was not: the index gives **born 20 July, baptised 21 July**, and the entry sits under the *next* date heading, below the crop. Reading further down the same page:

> **«Die 21 July 1757 — Jacobum Vincentium filium legitimum Valentini, et Helenæ jugalium Defranceschi, natum 20 hujus, baptizavit D. Carolus Simon Bertoni, Patrini fuere Ill.mus D. Emanuel de Perretti, et Ill.ma D.na Elisabeth Bono.»**

**Two things beyond the name.** The godparents are styled ***Illustrissimus*** and ***Illustrissima*** — de Perretti and Bono are Fiume patrician names, and a Carnian immigrant's son does not get those sponsors by accident eighteen years after being made a citizen. And the child is **the tenth son**, which is the number the family has always given and the number this archive could not reach while it had fourteen children.

*doc — [image](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99F-WWGH).*

rows.src: Fiume burials, September 1757, entry 14
rows.what: Whether Aloysia was really «born and buried 1757», since that cannot stand beside a brother born in July of the same year
rows.got:
**She was four years old, so she was born about 1753 and the conflict disappears.**

The frame is an Italian burial book, numbered, each entry *«d’anni X, figlia di …, sepolta con Bara nella …»*, under a **Settembre 1757** heading. Entry 14:

> **«Alovisia d’anni 4, figlia di Valentino, ed Elena Defranceschi, sepolta nella Tomba di …»**

**The unit is deliberate.** Entries on the same page that record infants give months — *«Maria di mesi 3»* two lines above — so «d’anni 4» means four years, not four months. The digit was magnified to be sure of it, and matches the «d’anni 4» of the entry immediately below.

**What it changes.** The archive had her as one of five infants «born and buried 1757». She was instead a child of about four, **born c. 1753**, and the 1757 date is her burial alone. *doc — [image](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99F-QD3H).*
ev: The Kvarner households — Rijeka and Bakar

rows.src: Maria's 1757 burial — the question Aloysia's entry raised
rows.what: Whether Maria, like her sister Aloysia, was older than an infant when she was buried in 1757
rows.got:
**She was an infant — the register says months, not years — so Aloysia's case does not repeat. But the count is off by a few months at the other end.**

The frame is the same Italian burial book, under a **Maggio 1757** heading. Entry 20:

> **«20. Maria figlia di Valentio, ed Elena Defranceschi **di mesi …**, sepolta con S.B. nella Tomba di S. Giovanni.»**

**The unit is the whole answer.** Aloysia's entry, four months later in the same book, reads *«d’anni 4»*; Maria's reads *«di mesi»*. The clerk distinguishes the two, and the line above Maria's — another Maria, of Giovanni and Maria Babi — splits the difference with *«d’un anno e mè»*. So Maria Defranceschi died in her first year.

**The numeral itself will not resolve.** Magnified twice, it sits against the gutter shadow at the line's end and reads as one or two minims — **1, 6 and 11 are all possible and this archive will not choose between them.** That matters a little: buried in **May 1757**, an infant of eleven months was **born in 1756**, one of a month or six in **1757**. Her entry accordingly no longer claims a birth year.

*doc for the burial and for «di mesi»; the age in months and the birth year are unread.*

rows.src: Fiume, St Vitus baptisms, film 005497925 — read at four dates no index reaches
rows.what: The four children of Valentino Defranceschi whose baptisms appear in no index anywhere, and whose pages therefore rested on a reading nobody could check
rows.got:
**All four found, all four exactly where the 6 September reading said, and three of them gave up a birth date that reading had not recorded.**

**How the frames were found, since this is reusable.** Any image ark resolves to a film and a frame number: `/service/records/storage/dascloud/das/v2/3:1:<ARK>` returns `{"name":"005497925_00293"}` — film 005497925, frame 293. Feeding the eleven indexed children through that gives eleven dated frames, and the gaps between them can be interpolated to about a frame either way. The film's own `/children` endpoint is refused by their security service and **was not pushed at**; the ordinary browse route — `/search/film/005497925?i=<n>`, whose page title carries the `wc=` waypoint — gives the same list legitimately. The film holds several volumes: frames 1–205 under waypoint `9R2X-ZNT:…714201`, frames 206 onward under `9R2X-C62:…714501`. **Do not interpolate across the join** — the two volumes run at different rates, about 9 frames a year before it and about 12 after.

| child | frame | the entry |
|---|---|---|
| **Ignatius Francus Mattheus** | 126 | «Die 29 Julij 1745 — Ignatium Franc.um Matthæum filium legitimum **D.ni Valentini, et Helenæ jugalium De Franceschi**, **heri natum**» |
| **Vitus Joannes Baptista** | 228 | «Die 18 Junij 1751 — Vitum Joannem Baptistam filium legitimum **D.ni Valentini, et D.næ Helenæ jugalium Defranceschi**, baptizavit D. Petrus Eustachius … Decanus» |
| **Aloysius Rochus** | 257 | «Die 18 Augusti 1754 — Aloysium Rochum filium legitimum **D.ni Valentini, et Helenæ jugalium Defranceschi, natum 16 hujus**» |
| **Rosalia Francisca** | 272 | «Die 8 8bris 1755 — Rosaliam Franciscam filiam legitimam **D.ni Valentini et Helenæ jugalium Defranceschi, natam 3a hujus**» |

**Three new birth dates**, from the registers' habit of saying how long ago the child was born: Ignatius **28 July 1745** (*heri natum*, born yesterday), Aloysius Rochus **16 August 1754**, Rosalia Francisca **3 October 1755**.

**And something the index could never have shown.** By the 1750s the clerk writes **D.nus Valentinus** and **D.na Helena** — *Dominus*, not plain Valentino — and the godparents are styled ***Illustrissimus*** and ***Illustrissima***: in 1754 «Ill.mus D.nus Joannes Josephus Carolus Borghesi, et Ill.ma Domicella **Lib. Bar. de Benzoni**» — a **free baroness** — and in 1757 «Ill.mus D. Emanuel de Perretti, et Ill.ma D.na Elisabeth Bono». **The Carnian who was made a citizen in 1739 was having his children held at the font by the patriciate of Fiume fifteen years later.** That is a social fact, and it is only on the page.

*doc — every one of the fifteen children now cites the image it stands on. Item 126 is closed.*

rows.src: Crikvenica births 1896, read entry by entry — and the reason 1897 cannot be read at all
rows.what: Uršula Kovačina, daughter of Petar Kovačina the joiner and Marija Car of house 119 — the baptism that would prove Anton Rudolf's wife is the guard's granddaughter
rows.got:
**She is not there, and the years she is most likely to be in are not filmed. This closes the FamilySearch route and hands the question to Rijeka.**

**What was read.** Crikvenica **Births (Rođeni) 1859–1896**, waypoint `9R28-RMH:…391676801`, **images 673 to 697** — the whole of 1896, about a hundred and fifty births, six to a spread. Every parents' surname and every house number was read. The surnames are Car, Katnić, Matejčić, Župan, Lovrić, Brozičević, Grbičić, Škiljan, Veljacić, Jurinčić, over and over. **There is no Kovačina birth in Crikvenica in 1896 at all.**

**Two Uršulas turned up and neither is ours** — «Urša Marija» of Martin Car at house 102, and «Urša» of Gergo Zanković at house 125. The name was common in the parish, which is worth knowing before anyone reads a later book hopefully.

**And now the wall.** The parish's filmed birth volumes are **1815–1823, 1855–1858, 1822–1855** and **1859–1896**, and that is all. **Crikvenica births from 1897 onward are not on film.** Uršula's parents married on **28 November 1895**, so a first child before the autumn of 1896 is barely possible and none was registered; her sister **Josipa died at eighteen months in September 1898**, which puts Josipa's birth at about March 1897. **The whole plausible window for Uršula falls in the unfilmed years.**

**So the link stays inference, and the way to settle it is now named.** Neither the index (four hundred Kovačina rows, no Uršula) nor the film can reach her. The Crikvenica register for 1897–1902 is with the **Državni arhiv u Rijeci**, which is exactly what work-list **141**'s letter asks for. *nil — and the negative is worth as much as a hit, because it stops anyone reading 1896 again.*

rows.src: Zorica's own baptism entry, at the foot of the last filmed page
rows.what: An image and a citation for Zorica, born 14 December 1896 — found while reading the year for somebody else
rows.got:
**She is the last birth entered in the book, and the entry changes something the archive believed about the name.**

Reading 1896 for a Kovačina that is not there turned up a Defranceschi that is. The final entry on **image 696** is **Zorica**, *zakonita*, and her father is written **«Josip Defran=ceski Antonov»** — *klesar*, a stonecutter — with the household placed as **«Iz Istrije mjesto Gračišće, sad ovdje stanujući»**: from Istria, the place Gračišće, now dwelling here.

**Three things come out of it.**

**The spelling.** The surname is written **Defranceski** — magnified twice, the second line is c-e-s-k-i, no *ch*. This archive had dated that form to the twentieth century and the diaspora. **A Croatian priest wrote it in the home parish in 1896**, before anyone left. See the correction.

**The address.** There is **no house number**. Where every other family on the page has one, this one is entered by its origin — the register's way of marking incomers. Six years after Anton Rudolf was born at Klenovica 22, the family were still being written down as people from somewhere else.

**The trade, again.** *Klesar* — the same word used of Josip at Marija Stjepanka's baptism at Ledenice in 1892 and at Ivan's death in 1896, and the trade his father Antonius held at Gračišće in 1863. Three parishes, three clerks, one word.

*doc — [image](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-R9WZ-V), Crikvenica births 1859–1896, film image 696.*

rows.src: Johann Defranceschi of Gallignana, born 1833 — tried in the index and tried on the shelf
rows.what: The Gračišće baptism of 1833 that would give parents to the sailor in the three Kriegsarchiv files
rows.got:
**Neither route exists, and one of them this archive had told itself did.**

**The index first.** Every *Defranceschi* and *De Franceschi* birth in the Croatia collection with a year between **1825 and 1842** was pulled — forty-five rows. They sit at Kaštelir, Tar, Pola, Fiume, Tarsatica and a scatter of «Croazia, Austria». **There is no Gračišće entry among them, and no Johann or Giovanni born 1833 anywhere in the set.**

**Then the film — and here the archive was wrong about itself.** Work-list 135 said *«the Gračišće baptisms of 1833 are on film and readable from here»*. **They are not.** Gračišće is not a parish in the FamilySearch Croatia collection at all: a search of all thousand parish nodes returns only **Pazin**, **Stari Pazin** and **Lupoglav (Pazin)** for that corner of Istria, and none of their volume lists contains a Gračišće book. This archive's **own atlas already said so** — the Gračišće place record carries **`nfilms: 0`** — so the work-list note contradicted the map for days.

**Gračišće is one of the unfilmed parishes**, which is exactly the class this archive counted in September: *495 of the 1,151 books in the Pazin inventory are in parishes with no film at all*. Its registers are at **DAPA Pazin** and on the parish shelf, which is where everything this site holds from Gračišće — the 1863 baptism, the Status Animarum — already came from.

**So the route is the one that has already worked once.** DAPA Pazin refuses open-ended research but will search **a named register for a named person over a stated period** — they did exactly that on the Gračišće birth register, certified the copy and posted it to Queensland for 117 kuna. *«Johann/Giovanni Defranceschi, Gračišće, 1833»* is precisely that shape of request. *nil on both searchable routes — and the correction is worth more than the search was.*

rows.src: Svetvinčenat — which volumes are filmed, and where this archive's own reading had stopped
rows.what: Whether the castle parish can be read past 1707, where the September sweep of DGS 005497884 ended
rows.got:
**All ten volumes are on film, and the archive's own reading of them stops at 1707. Everything after that is open ground.**

Svetvinčenat sits in the collection at `9R2H-DPJ:391644801,392404501` with **ten volumes**:

| | |
|---|---|
| Births | **1568–1588** · 1589–1646 · 1663–1708, 1696–1698 · **1709–1764** · **1764–1791, 1815–1874** |
| Marriages | 1581–1589, 1622–1623 · **1762–1858, 1855–1895** |
| Deaths | 1791–1887 · 1887–1917 |

**Where this archive already is.** The nineteen openings of **DGS 005497884** read band by band in September cover **1666–1707**, plus the 1628 entry that moved the Istrian sequence. The **1709–1764** and **1764–1791** books are the next two on the shelf and had not been touched — which is why Antonio of 1780, from *Atti* 48, was still only a footnote.

**Two limits worth recording.** The **1568–1588 volume is damaged**: the film's own card reads *«TORN PAGE(S) / POTRGANA STRANICA»* and the leaf photographed is a torn wedge missing about a third of its text. And the **DAPA inventory marks all five of the old birth books «digitised: no»** (nos 4841–4845) while FamilySearch has filmed them — a reminder that the inventory's digitised column and the film are two different questions.

*yield — the shelf mapped and the gap in this archive's own reading located.*

rows.src: Svetvinčenat baptisms 1780 — the first pages of the 1764–1791 book read here
rows.what: Whether the surname the *Atti* article calls the castle's only continuous one is actually in the parish register, and whether Antonio of 1780 is a real man on a page
rows.got:
**Both households are there, a fortnight apart, in the exact year the article names — and one of them is Antonio's.**

Svetvinčenat is **unindexed**: a search of the FamilySearch persona index for every spelling of the name, filtered to this parish, returns **zero rows**. The book has to be read — which is how this archive read 1666–1707 off DGS 005497884 in September. **This is the next book on that shelf**, and it had not been opened. **Births 1764–1791**, image 81 (`3:1:3QS7-899X-K3LW`), one frame, both pages:

> **«Anno D.ni 1780. Die 16 Aprilis S. Vincentij»** — Maria, daughter of Matthæus Pieder and Maria his wife; *«Patrini ad Sacrum Fontem fuere **Dominicus Defranceschi**, et **Fosca** Uxor ejus»*.

> **«Anno D.ni 1780 Die 1 Maij S. Vincentij»** — Joannes, son of Gregorius Mathes; among the godparents *«**Mathea uxor Antonij Defranceschi**»*.

**Two distinct households**, then: **Dominicus × Fosca** and **Antonius × Mathea**, both standing at the font in the castle parish within sixteen days of each other in 1780.

**And the second name is the one that matters.** *Atti* 48 has *«Guidati da **Antonio Defranceschi**, nel **1780** avevano ottenuto l'esonero dal partecipare alla difesa armata»* — led by Antonio Defranceschi, in 1780 the castle's families got themselves excused armed defence duty. **The register has an Antonius Defranceschi at S. Vincenti in 1780**, with a wife and a place in the parish's godparent circuit. The article's leader stops being a footnote in an Italian journal and becomes a man in a book.

**What this is not.** Neither entry is a **Defranceschi baptism** — both are appearances as godparents, which is how a household first shows itself in a register but is not the same as its own children. And **nothing here ties these two to the Gologorica–Gračišće line**; these are two more households of a surname this parish already holds in quantity — the archive has **seventy-five people at Svetvinčenat** and *«at least twelve distinct fathers of this surname in one small town between 1657 and 1737»*. What is new is that they are **after 1707**, where the earlier sweep stopped. *doc for both entries; the descent is not claimed.*

*(A misreading caught on the way: Antonius's wife was first read as «Fabria» from the full-page view. Magnified, the hand is plainly **Mathea**.)*
ev: The Svetvinčenat line — reading the register page by page

rows.src: Svetvinčenat births 1709–1764 — the volume's own index, and then the page it points to
rows.what: A Defranceschi household in the castle parish before 1780 — their own children, not godparent appearances
rows.got:
**Found: Cattarina, daughter of Sig.r Batta de Franceschi and Anzoletta, born 10 February 1728. That is fifty-two years before Antonio's exemption, and it is the family's own child.**

**The shortcut is the finding behind the finding.** Reading 216 register frames for one surname is not sensible; the volume carries **its own contemporary index** at the back, images ~197–214. It is arranged **by the child's forename**, not by surname, each line reading *«‹Given› di ‹father's forename› ‹SURNAME› ‹date› — c. ‹carta›»*. Sixteen images replace two hundred. On those frames an index leaf faces a register leaf, so **both pages of each frame have to be read**.

On the **C** page, second line:

> **«Cattarina fig.a di D.o Batta Defranceschi 11 Feb.ro 1728 — c. 66»**

**And carta 66 is on image 77, right page**, under the heading *«Adi 5 Febbro 1728»*:

> **«Catta[rina] fig.a leg.ma di S.r Batta de Fran.chi et di Anzoletta sua Consorte, nata li 10 d.to, fu battegata da me Arcip.te Quelis; Padrini furono al S. Fonte il S.r Bortolo Francal Giudice et la S.ra Madalena moglie del Sig. Vic.o Quelis.»**

**What the entry carries beyond the names.** The father is **«S.r» — Signore**, and so is the mother's style; the godfather is **Bortolo Francal, the Giudice**, the village's own magistrate, and the godmother is the **Vicar's wife**. A household that stands at the font with the judge and the vicar's wife is not a cottager's. That is the same social register as the 1754 Fiume baptism where a **free baroness** held Valentino's son — and the two families are not known to be connected.

**On the spelling.** The register abbreviates the surname **«de Fran.chi»**; the index writes it out as **«Defranceschi»**. Both forms are the same clerk's parish, twenty years apart, and the index is the one that spells it.

**The mother's name was read twice.** «Anzoletta» — the Venetian diminutive of Angela — only resolved when the line's right-hand end was magnified against the gutter; a first pass had it as «…ica».

*doc — [image](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99X-KQK2), Svetvinčenat births 1709–1764, film image 77, carta 66; index entry at image 199.*

rows.src: Svetvinčenat, the D page of the index — and the same man again thirty-two years later
rows.what: A second Defranceschi household in the castle, and whether any of these people can be followed across a lifetime
rows.got:
**A second father, a second child — and that child turns up again as a grown man standing godfather in 1764.**

The index's **D** page (image 200, right), eighth line:

> **«Dom.co Gasparo di Giacomo Defranceschi 9 Ag.to 1732 — c. 80»**

So beside **Batta** and Anzoletta, whose Cattarina was born in 1728, the castle holds **Giacomo Defranceschi**, whose son **Domenico Gasparo** was baptised on **9 August 1732**.

**And the register leaf facing that very index page closes the circle.** The same frame carries baptisms of **February 1764**, and in the entry of 9 February the godfather is

> **«D. Gasparo de Franceschi figlio di Giacomo»**

— *Gasparo de Franceschi, son of Giacomo*. **That is the child of 1732, aged thirty-one, standing at the font himself.** Two independent entries in one volume, thirty-two years apart, give the same man twice: once as an infant with his father named, once as an adult with the same father named.

**What the castle now holds, on the page:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Batta de Franceschi × Anzoletta** | daughter **Cattarina**, born 10 Feb 1728, carta 66 |
| **Giacomo Defranceschi** | son **Domenico Gasparo**, 9 Aug 1732, carta 80 |
| **Gasparo de Franceschi, son of Giacomo** | godfather, 9 Feb 1764 |
| **Dominicus Defranceschi × Fosca** | godparents, 16 Apr 1780 |
| **Antonius Defranceschi × Mathea** | godmother, 1 May 1780 |

**Fifty-two years of the name in one parish, from two fathers, without leaving a single volume.** Whether Dominicus of 1780 is the Domenico Gasparo of 1732 is the obvious question and **this archive will not answer it from a forename**; the 1764 entry shows the man was called *Gasparo*, not *Domenico*, by the people who knew him.

*doc — [image](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-KQS3) for the index line and the 1764 entry, both on film image 200; carta 80 itself not yet opened.*

rows.src: Svetvinčenat index, letters C to G read — the castle household takes shape
rows.what: Every Defranceschi line in the 1709–1764 index, read letter by letter
rows.got:
**Five of the index's letters are read. Three Defranceschi children, two fathers, and a naming pattern that points at a grandfather nobody has met.**

The **G** page gives the earliest yet:

> **«Gasparo di Batta Defranceschi 10 Agosto 1718 — c. 31 t°»**

written out in full, *Defranceschi*, not the register's clipped *de Fran.chi*.

**The household so far, all from the index unless marked:**

| father | child | date | carta |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Batta** | **Gasparo** | 10 Aug 1718 | 31 t° |
| **Batta** × **Anzoletta** | **Cattarina** | 10 Feb 1728 | 66 — *entry read* |
| **Giacomo** | **Domenico Gasparo** | 9 Aug 1732 | 80 |

**Two fathers, and each names a son Gasparo.** In a parish where godparents are the judge and the vicar's wife, that is the ordinary Venetian habit of naming the first son for his grandfather — which would make **Batta and Giacomo brothers, sons of a Gasparo who is older than this volume**. *That is an inference from a naming pattern and nothing else; the 1663–1708 book, if it carries an index of its own, is where it would be tested.*

**Letters read: C, D, E, F, G.** The E page — fifty-odd Elenas and Euffemias — is clean, and so is F. **Still unread: A, B, I, L, M, N, O, P, R, S, T, V, Z**, which is where Antonio, Domenico, Zuanne, Maria, Nicolò and Pietro would sit if they are there. **Carta 31 t° and carta 80 have not been opened.**

*doc for the three index lines and for the 1728 entry on carta 66; the 1718 and 1732 entries are known from the index only.*

rows.src: Svetvinčenat index, the B page — a third child, the father's full name, and a look-alike that dissolved
rows.what: The B section of the 1709–1764 index, where Battista and Bortolo would sit
rows.got:
**One more child, the father's name in full at last — and one line that looked like the name and is not.**

**The hit.** Second from the foot of the **B** page:

> **«Battistina fig.a di Gio Batta Defranceschi 23 Xbre 1731 — c. 76 t°»**

So the father this archive has been calling **«Batta»** from the 1728 entry is **Gio Batta — Giovanni Battista**, and he has a third child: **Battistina, 23 December 1731**, named for himself.

**The household as it now stands:**

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **Gio Batta × Anzoletta** | Gasparo | 10 Aug 1718, c. 31 t° |
| | **Cattarina** | 10 Feb 1728, c. 66 — *entry read* |
| | Battistina | 23 Dec 1731, c. 76 t° |
| **Giacomo** | Domenico Gasparo | 9 Aug 1732, c. 80 |

**The miss, and it is worth writing down.** Five lines into the same page:

> «Battista fig.o di m.ro Piero **Defranzieri** 7 mag.o 1712 — c. 12»

Magnified against the Battistina line on the same page, the two endings are plainly different: **‑eschi** with its *ch* on one, **‑ieri** with a clear *r* on the other. **Defranzieri is a different surname**, and at a glance in a list it reads exactly like this one. Anyone sweeping these books should expect it. *The archive counts it as dissolved, not as a variant.*

**Letters now read: B, C, D, E, F, G.** Still to do: **A**, and **I, L, M, N, O, P, R, S, T, V, Z**.

rows.src: Anzoletta — whose wife? The 1728 entry against the archive's own 1733 line
rows.what: Whether Anzoletta is the wife of Gio Batta or of Giacomo Defranceschi, because this archive now says both
rows.got:
**Two readings, both in this archive, and they do not agree.**

The families page has long carried, from the index, *«**1733** Maria, of **Giacomo and Anzoletta**»* among the twelve fathers of the name at Svetvinčenat.

The carta 66 entry read on 20 September says *«Catta fig.a leg.ma di S.r **Batta** de Fran.chi et di **Anzoletta** sua Consorte, nata li 10 d.to»* — **1728**.

**So Anzoletta is given to two different husbands five years apart.** Three readings are possible and the archive will not pick one from a forename:

1. **Two women of the name.** Anzoletta is the Venetian diminutive of Angela and common; two households of one surname in one small town could easily hold two.
2. **A misreading on carta 66.** «Batta» and «Giacomo» do not look alike, but the entry is abbreviated and the archive has been wrong on a forename before.
3. **A remarriage.** Gio Batta's last known child is **Battistina, 23 December 1731**; Giacomo's first is **Domenico Gasparo, 9 August 1732**. That is **seven and a half months** — too short for a widow to remarry and bear a child, so if it is a remarriage the 1732 child is not hers, and the 1733 Maria might be. *Thin, but not impossible.*

**What settles it** is carta 80 for the 1732 baptism and the 1733 entry behind the families page's line: both name the mother. **Neither has been opened.** Until they are, this archive holds two Anzolettas and says so rather than quietly merging them.

*pending — and flagged because a silent merge here would invent a household.*

rows.src: The mothers of the Svetvinčenat children — got from the index, not the film
rows.what: Who the wives were behind Gio Batta and Giacomo, and whether the two Anzolettas are one woman
rows.got:
**Four index entries answer it, and they turn a name-clash into a remarriage.**

A date-filtered sweep of the persona index for **1710–1740** — no place filter, because Svetvinčenat entries carry *«Croazia, Austria»* and nothing else, the failure this archive documented in the «Pula 1667» work — returns four rows for this household:

| child | father | mother | date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Maria | **Batta Franceschi** | **Anzoletta** | 5 Jul 1715 |
| Domenico Gasparo | **Giacomo De Franceschi** | **Maria** | 2 Apr / 9 Apr 1731 |
| Maria | **Giacomo Defranceschi** | **Anzoletta** | 4 Nov 1733 |
| Casparg *(Gasparo)* | **Jacobo De Franceschi** | **Anzola** | 26 Dec 1737 |

**Gio Batta × Anzoletta is confirmed thirteen years before carta 66** — a daughter Maria in 1715. And **Giacomo had two wives**: **Maria**, who bears Domenico Gasparo in April 1731 and then vanishes from the book, and **Anzoletta / Anzola**, who bears from November 1733.

**Which makes the timing fit exactly.** Gio Batta's last child is **Battistina, 23 December 1731**, and the household stops. Giacomo's first wife bears in **April 1731** and stops. Giacomo's second marriage produces a child in **November 1733**. **Two Defranceschi households are widowed within a year of each other, and the surviving husband of one marries the surviving wife of the other.** *That is the reading; it is inference, and this is what would prove or break it — nothing.* **Svetvinčenat's marriage register is not filmed between 1623 and 1762**, so the wedding itself cannot be reached, and a dispensation for affinity, if Batta and Giacomo were brothers, would have been recorded in exactly that gap.

**A misreading of mine that this corrects.** The volume's own D-page line was read here as *«9 Ag.to **1732**»*. The index of the same baptism gives **9 April 1731**, and the roster has carried 1731 all along. **The month and the year were both misread**; the abbreviated *Ap.le* was taken for *Ag.to*. Carta 80 would settle it on the page.

*doc for the four index rows; the remarriage is inf and labelled so.*

rows.src: Joining the corpus by household — 2,251 index rows swept and cross-matched
rows.what: Whether the disconnected people in this archive can be joined to each other mechanically, rather than one register page at a time
rows.got:
**Fifty-nine candidate generational chains, and a four-generation one at Rijeka that runs straight into this archive's own Fiume household.**

**The sweep.** Every persona-index row for *Defranceschi*, *De Franceschi* and *Franceschi* in the Croatian church books, on `q.surname` and `q.fatherSurname`, paged out: **2,251 deduped rows**, of which **1,380 name both parents**. `q.motherSurname` adds nothing — the mother is indexed under her maiden name, so the surname never matches.

**The method.** Fold each name to a consonant skeleton (so *Caralipeo*, *Caralipco*, *Carlipeo* and *decaralipeo* collapse to one woman), fold place exonyms (**Vitipolis = Fiume = Rijeka**; *Almissa = Omiš*; *Fasana = Fažana*; *Pola = Pula*), then look for a **child in one entry who becomes a father in another** — same parish, twenty to forty-five years later.

**The Rijeka chain, four generations deep:**

> **Giuseppe Defranceschi × Francesca**
> → **Valentino**, b. 1772 — who fathers **twenty-one indexed children** on **Ursula / Orsola** between **1794 and 1805**
> → **Franciscus**, b. 1797 — who fathers four more between **1833 and 1836**

Each generation is attested by index entries that name the father, and the chain closes on itself: Valentino appears as a child of Giuseppe *and* as the father of twenty-one, under five spellings of his own name (*Valentino*, *Valentinus Franciscus Xaverius*, *Valentinum Josephum Gregorium*) that the skeleton-fold brings together.

**Two more that stand up:**

* **Pula** — **Vittorio → Natale Mattio** b. 1816 → **Vittorio Giovanni** 1849. The grandson carries the grandfather's name, which is the pattern this archive already reads at Svetvinčenat.
* **Ližnjan** — **Mattio → Antonio** b. 1819 → eight children 1844–1859.
* **Omiš** — **Francesco → Giovanni** b. 1854/55/57 → eight children 1879–1892.

**And the question it raises, which this archive cannot answer today.** The Fiume household at the centre of the [Valentino page](/fiume-1626/#valentino) is **Valentino the Carnian**, made a citizen in 1739, with fifteen children between 1737 and 1757. The Rijeka chain starts with a **Giuseppe × Francesca** whose son is named **Valentino** and born about 1772. **A Valentino at Fiume in 1772 named for a Valentino at Fiume a generation earlier is exactly what a grandson looks like** — but **there is no Giuseppe among the fifteen**, and this archive has just been reminded (by Jacobus Vincentius, found this morning) that the fifteen were fourteen until today. *inf, and deliberately not asserted: the Fiume baptisms of 1758–1775 would settle whether Giuseppe is a sixteenth child.*

*doc for the index rows; the chains are **inf** — name, parish and a plausible age gap, not a stated parentage.*

rows.src: The roster audited against itself — how much of the corpus is one person entered twice
rows.what: Whether the «disconnected people» are really disconnected, or duplicates of each other arriving from different sources
rows.got:
**A good deal of it is duplication, and the rest divides into two very different problems.**

Folding all 1,221 roster rows on name, birth year, canonical place and maiden name:

* **38 groups, 83 rows, of which 45 would collapse** — same person, same place, arriving from two or three different sources. The commonest pairs are **household + myheritage** (17), **myheritage + record** (15) and **burial + myheritage** (9). *Pietro De Franceschi b. 1734 of Vodnjan is in the roster **seven times**.*
* **21 cross-place candidates** — same name and year in two places. Some are certainly one person: **Anton Rudolf b. 1890 «Klenovica | Ledenice»** is the man this archive re-read this morning, and Klenovica is *in* Ledenice parish; **Antonio b. 1897 «Middle Village | Queens»** — Middle Village is in Queens; **Camillo b. 1868 «Gologorica | Pazin»**, plus a third row at Poreč. Others — **Antonius b. 1848 «Gologorica | Pula»**, **Joannes b. 1871 «Gologorica | Ližnjan»** — are either a real move or a collision, and would each take a register to settle.
* **84 roster rows have no `/who/` page**, 63 of them from the index. **Those people cannot be linked to by anything**, because there is nothing to link to. That is the cheapest unconnectedness in the archive to fix.

**One thing the audit must not do is merge on its own.** «Maria Defranceschi b. 1757» looks like seven duplicates and is not: the rows are *Browachio*, *Buman*, *Contossich*, *Covaz*, *Dobrez* — **seven different women who married into the name at Rijeka**, distinguished only by the maiden name in brackets. And «Camillo De Franceschi, in Croatian» is a deliberate namesake row, not a stray. **The list is a worksheet, not a licence.**

*The full audit — all three lists — regenerates from `scratchpad/joins.py`.*

rows.src: Fiume baptisms, 23 November 1772 — read instead of the forty-four frames
rows.what: Whether Giuseppe × Francesca, whose son heads the Rijeka chain, belong to Valentino the Carnian's household
rows.got:
**A Helena Defranceschi stands godmother to Giuseppe's first son. That is what a grandmother does.**

The plan was forty-four frames of 1746–1750 hunting a Giuseppe. **One page answered more.** The index gives Giuseppe × Francesca **four children at Fiume** — 1772, 1774, 1776, 1778 — and the eldest son's entry is where a Fiume clerk names the company. Film image ark `3:1:3QS7-899F-WCFK`:

> **«Die 23.tia 9bris 1772.** Valentinus Franciscus Xaverius, filius legitimus **DD. Josephi, et Franciscæ jugalium Defranceschi**, heri natus, baptizavit C.us Lumaga, Levantibus D.no Francisco Tomassich **et D.na Helena Defranceschi**.»

**Valentino the Carnian's wife was Helena.** She bore fifteen children between 1737 and 1757, so in November 1772 she would be in her mid-fifties — alive, and exactly the age to hold a grandson at the font. **Godparents are the one category no index carries**, which is why this needed the page and why nobody had seen it.

**Two smaller things on the same line.** The father is **«DD.»** — the doubled *Dominus* of rank; and the celebrant is **Canonicus Lumaga**, the same name as the **«D.nus Canonicus Antonius Jacobus Lunaga»** who baptised Valentino's own son Aloysius Rochus in 1754. *One canon, two generations of the same household.*

**What it does not do.** It does not prove Giuseppe is Valentino's son. There could be another Helena Defranceschi at Fiume in 1772, and this archive has been wrong today about exactly this kind of confidence. **What it does is move the question from a naming coincidence to a person in the room.** *inf — strong, specific, and on the page.*

**The forty-four frames are still worth reading**, because a Giuseppe baptised in the 1746–1750 silence would settle it outright. *doc for the entry; inf for the descent.*
