**A third test now asks about the province**, and it was verified against the data as it stood this morning: **eight before, none after.**
rows.internalWhy: An audit of this archive's own data, not a finding about the family. Its home is /method/, which is a log by design.

rows.src: Fifteen years of Svetvinčenat that neither the index nor any reading had touched
rows.what: Svetvinčenat Births 1709–1764, film 005497885 — the indexed coverage tested, and image 161 read
rows.got:
**The archive's 114 Svetvinčenat people have a hole in them, and it is the index's hole, not the family's.**

Sorting them by how they were found: the **ark-backed** rows — the ones with a FamilySearch record behind them — run **1666 to 1737**, and then stop. The next is a **burial of 1758**; the next indexed **birth** is **1769**. *Twenty-one years with no indexed record of the name at all.*

**The family did not pause.** Three children in that window are already on this roster and every one of them was **read off a page by eye** — 1753, 1756, 1759. The register was always full; only the index stops.

**And 1738–1752 had been touched by nobody at all** — not the index, not any reading here. Fifteen years, in the parish where *Atti* 48 says this surname alone was continuous in the castle, immediately before the generation that won the exemption of 1780.

**The volume is film 005497885, *Births 1709–1764*, 214 frames** (waypoint `9R2H-RM8`). Anchored by reading: **image 126 = 1740**, **image 161 = 1752**, so the hole is roughly **images 118–162**, about four frames to the year.

**Image 161 was read, both pages, and it paid at once:**

> **«Die 15 Februarij 1752.** *Irena filia legitima **Matthæi Defranceschi**, et **Francisca** ejus legitimæ uxoris **ambo ex hac Parochia**, nata die 11 currentis… baptizata fuit a R.do Michaele Cassanovich; patrini fuerunt Zorzi (?) Lanich, et Maria uxor Joannis Valentich.»

**A child in no index anywhere**, and with her a household — *Matteo × Francesca*, **both of this parish**, so neither of them an incomer.

**And a second household on the same frame.** Twice in 1752 a godmother is entered as the wife of **Jacobo Defranceschi** — *«Franca Marcario uxor Jacobi Defranceschi»* on 26 March, *«Francisca uxor Jacobi Defranceschi»* on 17 December. **Two households of the name at the castle in one year**, which is what *«l'unico ad avere una continuità»* looks like from inside the register.

*One frame of about forty-five. The rest is a read, and it is now a specified one.*

rows.src: The first frames of the Svetvinčenat gap, and a set of twins nobody had counted
rows.what: Svetvinčenat Births 1709–1764, film 005497885, images 115–117 — October 1737 to May 1738, both pages
rows.got:
**Three frames at the front of the gap, and the name is on all three.**

**26 December 1737 — twins.** *«…baptizavit **duos infantulos geminos natos hodie mane a Jacobo de Franceschi, et Anzola ejus legitima uxore ambobus ex hac Parochia**, quibus fuit positum nomen, uni [Cesare?] alteri **Antonij**»* — two boys born that morning and baptised the same day, godparents **Natale Zanzevich (?)** and **Clara, widow of Bartolomeo Braccato**. **In no index anywhere.** *The second name is not read cleanly and no person has been invented out of it: the twin is recorded as existing and unnamed.*

**And a man the archive had never met, known only by the word *defuncti*.** On **7 October 1737** a godmother is *«Maria **filia defuncti Joannis Baptistæ de Franceschi**»* — a **Giovanni Battista of the name, dead by that autumn**. This roster already carries a *Maria di **Batta** Defranceschi, born 1716*, read off a page of this parish; **a woman of twenty-one is exactly who stands godmother in 1737**, so the two are very probably one. *(inf.)*

**Jacobo is the settled man of these years** — godfather on 27 November 1737, 12 January 1738 and 16 February 1738 — and **Maria is the settled woman**, godmother three times in 1737, once for a foundling *«dicta Jokto ex Albona, et Florente incognito»*.

**One thing is deliberately left open.** Jacobo's wife is **Anzola** in 1737 and **Francisca Marcario** in 1752. *Either he remarried, or there are two Jacobos, father and son. The doubt is written on the row instead of being resolved by preference.*

**Four frames of about forty-five now read** — 115, 116, 117 and 161 — *and every one of them has carried the name.* The gap is not thin; it is unread.

rows.src: A third household at Svetvinčenat, and three wives for one Jacobo in ten months
rows.what: Svetvinčenat Births 1709–1764, film 005497885, images 118, 119 and 121 — June 1738 to March 1739, both pages
ev: What a godparent line is worth
rows.got:
**A third household, and a warning about how to read the other two.**

**27 July 1738:** *«baptizavit unam infantulam **natam 25 currentis a Petro de Franceschi, et Jacoba ejus legitima uxore ambobus ex hac Parochia**, cui positum fuit nomen **Anna Euphemia**»*. Godparents **Blasius Marsoni, smith**, and **D.na Margarita**. **In no index.** So inside the unread fifteen years there are now **three households of the name** — Jacobo's, Pietro's and Matteo's — in a parish of a few hundred souls.

**And then the register contradicts itself.** In ten months it gives *«uxor Jacobi de Franceschi»* **three different women**: **Anzola** at the twins' baptism in December 1737, **Agata** on 10 August 1738, **Jacoba** on 7 September 1738 — and then **Angela**, who is Anzola, on 1 March 1739. *Angela is alive on both sides of the other two.* **One man did not have three wives in ten months.**

**Either more than one Jacobo de Franceschi was living in the parish at once, or the godparent formula is unreliable about husbands.** There is a specific reason to suspect the second: ***Jacoba* is Pietro's wife six weeks before she is Jacobo's**, in an entry where she is a parent and the clerk was being exact. A hand writing *«Jacoba uxor Jacobi»* was probably pulled by her own name.

**Neither reading is preferred.** [The rule that came out of it](/method/) is that a *«wife of X»* in a godparent line shows a household existed and must never be used to decide which household somebody was in.

**Coverage, said plainly.** Images **115–119 and 121** are read. **Image 120 is not** — its signed link expired before it was fetched. And **image 121's left page carries a loose slip of paper laid on the book when it was filmed**, which hides part of two entries; neither is a Defranceschi entry, but the page is **not** a clean nil and is not recorded as one.

rows.src: The Vienna catalogue searched again under the spellings the stem cannot reach
rows.what: ÖStA Archivinformationssystem — the -ski and -zeschi spellings, which «contains Franceschi» cannot match
rows.got:
**Yesterday's rule was «search the stem». The stem has a hole in it.**

*«Contains **Franceschi**»* catches *Defranceschi*, *De Franceschi* and the *-ini* diminutives in one pass — but **it cannot match a spelling with a k or a z**, and this family has both. Three records fall out of the spellings it misses:

· **Defranceski, Humbert** — ***«Geburtsort: Pola · Beruf: Schiffbauer»***, a **Landsturminfanterist** in a **military court case at Belluno, 1918** (`KA MGA GS B Belluno Gerichtsfälle GEx Innichen K 887/18`). **A shipwright out of Pula, in front of a military court in the Dolomites in the last year of the war** — and a birthplace that lands on this archive's southern-Istrian line.
· **Defranzeschi, Heinrich, born 9 July 1912** — a wartime card, `AdR MilEv ZSK 11.6`.
· **Franzeschi**, 1814 — `AVA Inneres PHSt 374.1814`, a police-directorate file with no forename.

**So the working rule is corrected rather than repeated.** Searching one stem is right for *-schi*; **the surname needs three**: *Franceschi*, *Franceski*, *Franzeschi*. *One query found 99 records and missed a man whose birthplace is in this archive's own gazetteer.*

*Still untried: the **đ** spelling (Defranđeski) and Franzeski. Neither is likely in a Vienna catalogue, but neither has been run.*

rows.src: Two Giovanni Battistas at Svetvinčenat, and the loose slips turn out to be records
rows.what: Svetvinčenat Births 1709–1764, film 005497885, images 120 and 122 — March to June 1739, both pages
rows.got:
**The forename problem is not confined to the Jacobos.**

**19 April 1739:** *«Patrini fuere **Joannes Baptista de Franceschi**, et Clara vidua defuncti Bartholomei Braccato»* — **a Giovanni Battista of the name, alive, at the font**. Eighteen months earlier, on 7 October 1737, the same register wrote *«Maria filia **defuncti** Joannis Baptistæ de Franceschi»*. **Two men, one name, one small parish**, and father-and-son is the ordinary explanation.

**Said carefully, because of where it points.** The Fiume question this archive has spent the week on turns on **a Joannes Baptista de Franceschi of unknown origin** fathering a child there in 1748. *A man of that name alive at Svetvinčenat in 1739 is a name in the right decade and nothing more. No document joins them. It is written down as something to test, not as a link* — and the register has just finished demonstrating how cheap a forename is here.

**Jacobo goes on being everyone's godfather** — 13 April and 7 June 1739, on top of the four already recorded.

**And the coverage caveat published this morning is withdrawn.** **Image 120 is a second exposure of image 121's opening**, book page 107, with the **loose slips in different positions**, so the opening reads complete. **The slips are the priest's own memoranda** — baptisms written in Italian on scraps and kept in the Latin register, photographed where they lay. *They are records; neither names this family.* [Filed as method](/method/), and [corrected](/corrections/).

rows.src: David's own citations, diffed against the site, and read
rows.what: The 351 arks in David's citation files against every ark the site carries
rows.got:
**Ten arks of David's own were never read into this archive, and three of them are records.**

· **Vittoria Defranceschi, born 29 April 1894 at Telve** in the Valsugana, daughter of **Antonio Defranceschi** and **Rosa Mattivi** — Trento diocesan registers, page 251, film 001388687.
· **Estefania Defranceschi, married at Dallas, Texas on 24 July 2004**, aged twenty-seven, to **Lance C Thomas** — the latest-dated record of the name here.
· One that **cannot be opened at all**: *«This record can only be displayed on certain accounts.»* Signing in does not help; the owner has restricted it.

**A fourth was already here and gained something.** *Marina De Franceschi, 1710* was read off a Svetvinčenat page by eye with no ark; the index entry behind it is `1:1:X9DP-3HTQ`, and it names her mother — **Vittoria** — whom the page did not. **The eye-read and the index agree on everything else.**

**And the burial that started the week's Fiume work turns up twice.** *Maria Defranceschi, buried at Fiume on 2 August 1804, aged nought days, daughter of **Valentino and Orsola***, is indexed under two arks; both were already on the row, which is why the first count of the gap was too big. [The count is corrected](/corrections/).

*Seven of the ten are film images — register pages, a read rather than a fetch, and the next job.*

rows.src: Seven register pages David had cited and nobody had opened
rows.what: The seven film-image arks from David's citations — Kaštelir, Bakar and Parenzo, read on the plate
rows.got:
**Three households, in three towns, out of seven pages that were sitting in David's own citations and had never been opened here. None of the four films is referenced anywhere else in this archive.**

**Kaštelir — a tailor's house, and three generations of one name.** At **house 23** of *Castellier*:
· **«Franciscus Defranceschi, sartor — q.m Julii»**, dead **26 January 1892** of apoplexy, **aged 73 years 5 months** — born about August 1818, and *quondam Julii* gives his father, a **Giulio** already dead.
· **«Joannes Aloysius De franceschi»**, dead **18 November 1858 aged eight months** of *febris verminosa*.
· **«Josephus Defranceschi, sartoris»** — **son of the tailor** — dead **19 March 1870 aged eight** of angina.
*The 1858 entry says* agricola *and the 1870 one* sartoris*: either the trade changed in twelve years or the house held two families, and the archive records it as it stands.*

**Bakar — a widow born under Charles VI.** *«Vidua Catharina Defranceschi»*, **dead 7 April 1819 at house 121 of Buccari, aged eighty-five**, of old age, with all the sacraments. **Born about 1734** — the earliest-born person of the name this archive can place at Bakar. **And she was a widow**, so a Defranceschi husband was there before her and is still unnamed.

**Parenzo — a carpenter, and a marquis at the font.** *«**Parenzo li 28 Luglio 1846.** Paolo Francesco Domenico figlio delli giugali **Mattio Defranceschi falegn.** e **Domenica Frezza** nacque li 26 corr.»* — baptised by Canon Pietro Monfalcon, **godparents Francesco Marchese de Polesini and Ellena de Filippini-Coletti**, midwife Elena Weber. **The Polesini were the first noble house of Parenzo**, and a marquis of that family stood for a carpenter's son.

**The same couple's daughter, and probably her death.** **Anna Maria, born 20 October 1844, baptised 11 November.** Thirty-five years later the town's death register has *«17 Settembre 1879, casa 346 — Anna Maria Defranceschi, moglie di Giacomo Rocco fu Matteo»*, **aged 35**, of dropsy. *A woman born 20 October 1844 is thirty-four years and eleven months on 17 September 1879, which is what a clerk writes as thirty-five.* **doc for each record; inf for joining them.**

*Coverage, plainly: the Kaštelir and Bakar pages were read in full. At Parenzo, the left page of image 62 and both pages of image 309 were read; **the right-hand page of image 62 was read only as far as its first band**, and is not recorded as a nil.*

rows.src: A fourth Svetvinčenat household, and two Euphemias fourteen months apart
rows.what: Svetvinčenat Births 1709–1764, film 005497885, images 123 and 125 — June 1739 to October 1740, both pages
ev: Reading a year in this hand
rows.got:
**A fourth household of the name inside the unread years.**

**«Die 4 8bris 1739** … natam die 1ma currentis **a Batta Defranceschi et Jacoba ejus legitima uxore ambobus ex hac Parochia**, cui positum fuit nomen **Euphemia»** — godparents **D.nus Aloysius Spinotti** and **Ursula, wife of Francesco Marzoni**. ***Batta* is Battista**, and a Joannes Baptista de Franceschi was standing godfather in this same register five months earlier: *very probably his household.*

**And then the register does something it cannot explain.** On **27 July 1738** *«**Petro** de Franceschi et **Jacoba** ejus legitima uxore»* baptise **Anna Euphemia**. Fourteen months later *«**Batta** Defranceschi et **Jacoba** ejus legitima uxore»* baptise **Euphemia**. **Same mother's name, same daughter's name, two different fathers.** *Either two households were doing the same thing at once, or the first child died and the name was given again and one of the two fathers is misread. Both entries were magnified and both read as written; the tangle is published rather than tidied.*

**Angela settles down.** *«Angela uxor Jacobi Defranceschi»* stands godmother again in October 1739 — so Angela is Jacobo's wife in **1737, 1739 and 1739**, which makes the *Agata* and *Jacoba* of 1738 the odd ones rather than her.

**Petrus is at the font too**, godfather to a foundling on 10 June 1740.

**One reading hazard, caught before it was published.** The year headings on images 123 and 126 first read as **1759**; the entries beneath them are dated **1739**, and the page numbers run straight on from image 122. *In this hand a 3 and a 5 are the same stroke with a different lean — anchor a frame on an entry date and a page number, never on the heading.*

rows.src: The Austrian catalogue's last two spellings, and the near-duplicate households resolved
rows.what: ÖStA under Franzeski and the đ form; households.json near-duplicates read one by one
rows.got:
**The Vienna spelling sweep is finished and the last two stems are empty.** *Franzeski* — **no entries found**. *ranđesk*, for the Croatian **đ** form — **no entries found**. With *Franceschi* (99), *Franceski* (1) and *Franzeschi* (2), **five stems now cover every spelling this archive uses**, and the catalogue holds nothing else.

**And the near-duplicate households were read rather than left flagged.** Three pairs had carried a `nearDup` marker for days with nothing said about them:

· **h088 / h091 are not duplicates at all.** *Gulielmus **Lazzer** × Andrina Defranceschi* against *Matheus **Lazaro** × Lucia Defranceschi* — different husband, different wife, eleven years apart, and an in-law surname the index spells two ways. **Two men of one family married two women of this one.** The link is withdrawn.
· **h078 / h080** — one husband, *Paschalis Zanghirella*, a son *Petrus* in both, and a wife who is **Michaela** in one record and **Theresia Dominica** in the other.
· **h064 / h069** — a Defranceschi married to a **Bellinich** at Fiume in 1836 and again in 1849, the wife **Catharina** then **Carolina**. *Two sisters or one woman read twice; the entries do not say.*

**A fourth swapped household fell out of it** — *«Theresia Dominica De Franceschi × Paschalis Zanghirella»*, the wife in the father's slot, [missed that morning](/corrections/) because the forename list had *Paulus* and not *Paschalis*.

rows.src: Jacoba is Pietro's wife on both sides of the entry that gives her to a Batta
rows.what: Svetvinčenat Births 1709–1764, film 005497885, images 124, 127 and 128 — September 1739 to May 1741, both pages
rows.got:
**Three frames, no new baptism of the name — and one godparent line that moves a household.**

**29 December 1739**, a foundling named Agata, godparents *«Blasius Pustianaz, et **Jacoba uxor Petri Defranceschi**»*. **Jacoba is Pietro's wife.** She was Pietro's wife in **July 1738** too, when they baptised **Anna Euphemia**.

**Between those two, on 4 October 1739, the register gives her to a *Batta*** — *«a Batta Defranceschi et Jacoba ejus legitima uxore»*, baptising a daughter **Euphemia**. **So the one entry naming a Batta sits between two that name Pietro**, eleven weeks before and seventeen months after.

**The likeliest reading is now that the October child is Pietro and Jacoba's too**, and that the first Euphemia had died — the name given again, which is what these families did. *The entry still reads **Batta** under magnification and has not been altered. What has changed is which way it leans, and [the roster row now says so](/who/euphemia-di-batta-defranceschi-1739/).*

**Pietro and Jacobo go on being everybody's godparents** — Petrus at the font on 9 February 1740, Jacobus twice in November and December 1740.

*Read so far: 115–128, 161. Still: 129–160, 162.*

rows.src: Helena of 1742, and Jacoba is Pietro's wife for the third time
rows.what: Svetvinčenat Births 1709–1764, film 005497885, images 129–131 — May 1741 to August 1742, both pages
rows.got:
**A fifth child out of the unread years, and the Jacoba question settles further.**

**10 August 1742** — *«baptizavit unam infantulam, **natam die 5 currentis a Matthæo Defranceschi, et Francisca ejus legitima uxore ambobus ex hac Parochia**, cui positum fuit nomen **Helena**»*, godparent **Martinus Stancovich**. **In no index.**

**She gives the Matteo household a span.** Francisca is already *«uxor Matthei Defranceschi»* as a godmother on **27 August 1741**; Helena is born in **1742**; **Irena** follows in **1752**. *Eleven years of one family at the castle, entirely inside the stretch the index does not cover.*

**And Jacoba is Pietro's wife for the third time** — *«Jacoba uxor **Petri** Defranceschi»*, godmother on **16 February 1742**, after July 1738 and December 1739. **Three attestations to Pietro against one to a Batta**, and the one to a Batta sits in the middle of them. *The October 1739 Euphemia is now very probably Pietro and Jacoba's second daughter of that name.*

**Two names new to this archive.** **Casparus Defranceschi**, godfather 17 August 1741 — very likely the *Gasparo* born 1718 the roster already holds from the index, who would be twenty-three. And **Joanna Defranceschi**, godmother 30 June 1741, **entered under the surname in her own right** rather than as anyone's wife, which in this hand usually means an unmarried daughter of the house.

**Jacobo keeps turning up** — godfather again on 14 January 1742.

*And the page carries something that is not a baptism at all: **«Die 27 Maij 1741, In Castro S. Vincentij in Sacra Visitatione»**, the record of a bishop's visitation to the castle, signed by the chancellor **Vincenzo Baldini**.*

**Read: 115–131, 161. Still: 132–160, 162.**

rows.src: A Joannes Baptista de Franceschi «ex Cargna» standing at a Svetvinčenat font in 1742
rows.what: Svetvinčenat Births 1709–1764, film 005497885, images 132 and 133 — August 1742 to May 1743, both pages
rows.got:
**The best thing the gap has produced, and it is one line of a godparent entry.**

> **«Die 20 Xbris 1742.»** *…baptizavi unam infantulam **spuriam**, natam heri, a **Gregorio Bercar** et **Maria Simebich ex Parochia Barbana**, cui positum fuit nomen **Victoria**. **Patrini fuerunt Joannes Baptista de Franceschi, ex Cargn., et Maria uxor Gasparis Perlar.**

**He is the only person of this surname anywhere in this register who is given an origin.** Every other one is *«ambo ex hac Parochia»*, or nothing. **The clerk marked him because he was not local.**

***Cargna* is the Venetian form of *Carnia*** — and *«ex Carnia»* is the exact phrase the Fiume marriage register puts on **Valentino de Franceschi** on **28 February 1737**. **Joannes Baptista** is the forename at the centre of the Fiume question, where a man of that name and no known origin fathers a child there in **1748**.

**It is not claimed that these are the same man.** What it is: **the first document this archive has found placing the right surname, the right forename and a Carnian origin together inside Istria in the right decade.** *The word is abbreviated with a suspension stroke and was magnified three times; the letters are given as read and the expansion is flagged as inference.*

**It also unsettles what was already here.** Svetvinčenat has a Joannes Baptista **dead by October 1737** and another **standing godfather in April 1739**. *If the 1739 man is this one, the Battistas of this parish are themselves Carnian incomers — and the register does not say.*

**Elsewhere on the two frames:** Petrus Defranceschi godfather again on 29 December 1742; nothing of the name on image 133 (September 1742 – May 1743).

**Read: 115–133, 161. Still: 134–160, 162.**

rows.src: Casparus of 1743 sorts out his own father, and «ex Cargnia» is spelled in full
rows.what: Svetvinčenat Births 1709–1764, film 005497885, image 134 — March to July 1743, both pages
rows.got:
**A sixth child out of the gap, and he settles the question his family has been raising for four days.**

**15 June 1743:** *«**Casparus filius legitimus Jacobi Defranceschi, et Francisca ejus legitimæ uxoris, amborum ex hac Parochia** … natus die 1mo currentis»* — godparents **D.no Francisco Xaverio Profumo** and **D.na Catharina, daughter of Dominicus Louicini of Dignano**.

**Jacobo's wives stop contradicting each other once they are laid out.** *Anzola/Angela* — the twins of December 1737, godmother March and October 1739. *Francisca* — mother of Casparus in 1743, godmother twice in 1752, once as **«Franca Marcario»** with her maiden name. **The two do not overlap: Anzola ends in 1739, Francisca begins in 1743.** That is a widower and a second marriage, and the maiden name is on the later entry because the clerk knew which wife she was.

**And it disposes of *Agata* and *Jacoba*.** Both are *«uxor Jacobi»* in 1738, **inside the years Anzola is alive**, and neither recurs. **They are the clerk writing the wrong husband into a godparent line** — and *Jacoba* is Pietro's wife, now attested four times, the fourth on **29 June 1743**.

**The Carnian reading is confirmed by the register itself.** On **20 May 1743** the same hand writes *«Patrini fuerunt **Nicolaus Temperin ex Cargnia**, et **Antonio Defranceschi**»* — ***Cargnia* spelled out in full**, where the entry of 20 December 1742 had abbreviated it. *So «Joannes Baptista de Franceschi, ex Cargn.» is securely* ex Cargnia = Carnia — **and a Carnian stands at this font beside a Defranceschi.**

**Read: 115–134, 161. Still: 135–160, 162.**

rows.got:
**The marriage film's number had sat on the worklist as a blocker for days.** *It was never a catalogue problem.* **Each of these films opens with a target board photographed at the Croatian State Archives in Zagreb on 17 and 19 June 1997**, giving the register, the years, the item number, the roll and the operator in plain capitals.

| film | title of record | years | roll |
|---|---|---|---|
| 005497885 | Matična knjiga **krštenih** *(births)* | 1709–1764 | — |
| **005497886** | Matična knjiga **vjenčanih** *(marriages)*, item 1 | **1581–1623** | 88 |
| 005497887 | Matična knjiga **umrlih** *(deaths)* | 1859–1893 | 89 |

**And film 886 does not stop at 1623** — *frame 300 is a printed Austrian «Liber Copulatorum» ruled in columns and dated **1887**, so the marriage film runs across several items to at least that year.* **The 1762 volume begins at frame 43** and has **no index**, so it must be walked: frame 50 is 1765, frame 80 is 1778, frame 150 opens a new volume at 1815 — *about **2.3 frames to the year**.*

rows.src: One word, magnified against the clerk's own hand, moves a household by three years
rows.what: Svetvinčenat Births 1709–1764, film 005497885, image 134 re-read — and images 143, 147, 161 as controls
rows.got:
**This archive published the mother of Casparus 1743 as «Francisca» for five days. She is Pascasia.**

*Settled not by staring at the word but by finding **the same clerk writing both candidate names elsewhere in the same volume** and setting the three side by side at one magnification:* his **«Franciscus»** on the facing leaf (carta 119v, 8 October 1743) and his **«Pascasia»** nine images on (image 143, 31 March 1746). **The disputed word is the 1746 word stroke for stroke and shares two letters with «Franciscus».**

**Consequences.** *[h107] Jacobo × Pascasia begins **1743**, not 1746. And **1743 stops carrying the «two Jacobos» case** — there is one wife that year, not two, so the «eight days» argument collapses and the conclusion moves onto the 1752–53 evidence, which is of a better kind.*

**A second error in the same entry:** the godfather was published as *«Dominicus Xaverii Bosponi»*. He is **Francesco Saverio Profumo**, chancellor of the parish — *verified on three frames in three years, and the name was wrong in four files.*

rows.src: Twenty-two openings of the Svetvinčenat marriage register, and twelve of the name
rows.what: Svetvinčenat marriages, film 005497886, frames 43–64 — July 1762 to February 1773, about 170 marriages
rows.got:
**Read opening by opening at a scale that shows a whole spread at once, with anything promising taken to 5× before it was written down.**

**The acts of the name, in order:**
· **6 Nov 1762** — *«M.ro **Gasparo de Franceschi**»*, witness. **«M.ro» is Maestro** — the first trade-style recorded for any Defranceschi of this parish.
· **22 Oct 1765** — *«Domenico Calluzzi q.m Pietro … con **Pasqua Ved.a q.m Giacomo de Fran-/ceschi in 2di uoti**»*. **A widow remarrying, and the first dated death of any Jacobo here.**
· **9 Feb 1766** — *«Con **Elena figlia di q.m Mattio de Franceschi** nativa di questo Castello»*, marrying **Mattio Santalezza** of the Albona territory. **The first marriage of a person of the name this archive found.**
· **9 Jul 1766** — *«D.no **Gasparo de Franceschi**»*, witness.
· **13 Aug 1766** — *«**Gaspare de Franceschi q.m Ant.o ex hoc Castro**»*, witness. **A patronymic that excluded two of three candidates outright.**
· **10 Jun 1771** — *«**Dominicus de Franceschi** … cum **Victoria Trecento** … Testibus … ac **Victorio de Franceschi**»*. **A Defranceschi marrying with a Defranceschi standing witness.**
· **23 and 25 Nov 1771** — *«**Jacobo q. Jacobi de Franceschi**»*, witness twice in one week.
· **10 Jun 1772** — *«**Giacobus filius Giacobi de Franceschi**, et **Nicolina filia Nicolai Tes[s]ereti**»*.
· **Jan–Feb 1773** — *«**Ant.º de Franceschi**»* four times, and *«**Victorio de Franceschi filio Antonij**»* once.

**⚠ Not all of this was new, and the worklist had been calling it discovery.** *The 1772 marriage, the «Giacomo dead before 1771» and the 1773 witnessings were **already published** from earlier readings of frames 62–64. **The sweep confirmed all three at magnification and changed none** — which is worth recording, but it is verification.*

**Genuinely new: the 1771 marriage, the 1765 widowhood, the 1766 marriage, all three Gasparo witnessings and the 25 November 1771 second witnessing.**

**Frames 57–60 and 44–52 carry nothing of the name** — *about a hundred marriages of Percovich, Bulcich, Zadro, Venier, Mazzan, Justinaz, Angelich, Milcich, Stancovich. **A read-and-nil stretch is a finding in a one-name study**, and it is logged so it is not swept twice.*

rows.src: Croatia's newspaper portal, re-run — and a claimed absence that is not one
rows.what: Portal Stare hrvatske novine (dnc.nsk.hr) — «Defranceschi» and «Defranceski» across all digitised Croatian newspapers
rows.got:
**⚠ This was written as though the portal had never been opened. It had.** *[The source entry](/sources/) for `dnc-nsk` already recorded a completed search — **with the same hit counts, 46 and 4** — and its own findings: Zora Defranceschi nursing at Crikvenica in 1915, Antun and Viktor in the Gologorica riot trial of 1894, the «stancija Defranceschi». **This is a re-run, and it is logged as one.** What made it look new is that [worklist 90](/worklist/) carried the row as «pending» while the source entry beside it said «done» — and that the stored URL was `https://`, which the portal refuses. **It answers on `http://` only.**

**Fifty hits: 46 for «Defranceschi», 4 for «Defranceski».** *Across «Naša sloga», «Primorac», «Narodne novine», «Domobran», «L'Istria», «Galeb» (Bakar), «Pučki prijatelj» (Krk), «Slovinac», «Hrvatska vila» and the imperial gazette — **1845 to 1920**. Citations harvested to `data/harvest/dnc-nsk-newspapers.json`.*

**Three seams, and the first is the best.**

**1 · The «Aquilone» from the other side.** *About twenty of the hits are the Austro-Hungarian shipping columns of «Primorac», and they are the **same brig** [the at-sea page](/at-sea/) already follows through the British press — «Aquilone, Aus, 350, Defranceschi».* **The Croatian columns print the ports the British papers had no reason to:** *Constantinople (Sep 1873), **Cardiff → Venice (23 Aug 1876)**, Constantinople → Lošinj (Jan 1877), Venice ← Odessa (Feb 1877), Dedeagach → Genoa (Apr 1877).* **All twenty read the same day: Rochefort, Syra, Falmouth, Bristol, Odessa, Constantinople, Dedeagach, Venice, Trieste, Lošinj — and Newport for Guadeloupe in December 1877 and January 1878, which confirms in print the West Indies voyage the at-sea page had only inferred.** *The voyage table roughly doubles, from 22 rows to 42.*

**⚠ And one of them lands on a date this archive already cared about.** *She sailed **Falmouth → Bristol on 14 July 1876** and **Bristol → Cardiff on 9 August**, and **Emerico De Franceschi married Marietta Cosulich at St Peter's, Roath — the Catholic parish of Cardiff — on 26 July 1876**. **On the wedding day the ship lay at Bristol, not Cardiff** — across the water, and at Cardiff a fortnight later. **That is a convergence, not an identification**: the shipping column gives a surname and no forename, and the archive has never established who the Aquilone's master was. It is now the sharpest question the at-sea page has.*

**2 · A Defranceschi in the 1879 Istrian election, on the Italian side.** *«Galeb» (Bakar), 15 July 1879: dr. Klodić, the Croatian national candidate, «**podlegao Talijanu Defranceskiju**» — **defeated in the rural communes by the Italian Defranceski**. «Naša sloga» returns to it on 16 August and names the men of the Poreč district who went over «**dušom i tijelom za Defranceskia**».* **Which man is open** — Carlo de Franceschi is the obvious candidate and that is proximity, not proof.

**3 · Antun Defranceski, a Zagreb civil servant.** *«Narodne novine», 8 June 1863: appointed **accounting councillor**. «Domobran», 17 January 1865: a Defranceschi among the **officials of the royal building directorate**, subscribing a florin to a singing student. **Nothing ties him to any line here**, and he is recorded because a one-name study records the name where it falls.*

**On the terms, and a lesson from Trove.** *The portal permits **personal use and research work**, requires written permission for commercial use, and requires the credit line below. **The OCR was read for research; it is not reproduced here in bulk** — the findings are in this archive's own words, with short quotations.* © Portal Stare hrvatske novine, Nacionalna i sveučilišna knjižnica u Zagrebu, 2009.

rows.src: Eight spellings, not two — and the two I skipped held the best of it
rows.what: Portal Stare hrvatske novine (dnc.nsk.hr) — every spelling variant of the name, counted
rows.got:
**David asked whether I had tried all the name variations. I had tried two.**

| term | hits | |
|---|---|---|
| `Franceschi` | **68** | broad — other families too |
| `Defranceschi` | **46** | ✓ run |
| **`De Franceschi`** *(spaced)* | **20** | ✗ **skipped** |
| `Defranceski` | **4** | ✓ run |
| **`Defrančeski`** *(Croatian orthography)* | **3** | ✗ **skipped** |
| `Defrancheschi`, `Defranceschich` | 0 | |
| `Franceski` | *1332* | **noise** |

**⚠ `Franceski` is a trap.** *Croatian OCR renders **«francuski» — «French»** close enough to match it. **A count that large is a language, not a family.***

**⚠ And the spaced form is a different search, not a looser one.** *`De Franceschi` reaches **«L'Istria»**, the Istrian journal of 1846–52 — **six of its first ten results** — which the unspaced form barely returns.*

**What the two skipped spellings gave:**

· **«L'Istria», 9 May 1846** — *«**Perseveri, caro De Franceschi, ed in qualunque incontro raccolga quanto può memorie**»*. **Carlo de Franceschi being told, in print, to become the historian he became** — thirty-three years before «L'Istria: note storiche». The journal's **1847 index of contributors** lists him; its **1846 subscriber list** puts **two** of the name at **Pisino**.
· **«Pučki prijatelj» (Krk), 19 Dec 1919 and 27 Feb 1920** — *«**Defrančeski Antun**»* among the workers of the **Pula arsenal**, and *«**Defrančeski Ante**»* in a list *«sabrano u **Ližnjanu** kod Pule»*. **A working man on the Ližnjan line's own ground, invisible to every earlier sweep for want of one diacritic.**

**The rule.** *A one-name study's spelling list is not a preamble, it is **the instrument**. It belongs in the log with its counts, every time — because «every spelling» is what you write when you have stopped counting.* © Portal Stare hrvatske novine, Nacionalna i sveučilišna knjižnica u Zagrebu, 2009.

| **85** | 22 Nov 1779 | **Ant.o Defranceschi** witness — *«e di D.no Z.ne Volfe Testimonj»* |

**What the two acts of January 1779 change.**

**·** **Antonia is the daughter baptised 20 October 1747** to Jacobo and Pascasia — *thirty-one, and «q.m», her father dead, which agrees with Pascasia remarrying as a widow in 1765.* **She marries a Carnian**, the second on this film in five years.

**·** **Domenico is a widower**, so **Victoria Trecento died between 10 June 1771 and 13 January 1779** — *no year printable; Svetvinčenat's deaths before 1859 are on no film reachable here.*

**·** **Domenico is «M.ro», Maestro** — the second of the family styled so at the castle. *The craft is never named.*

**·** **⚠ Two Foscas.** *The April 1780 godmother «Fosca Uxor ejus» is **Fosca Placich**, not the Fusca who married a Jacomini of Parenzo in 1773. This archive was one step from conflating them.*

*(doc for every act above; the Carnian pattern is doc, what it means about descent is not claimed.)*

**⚠ 29 September — frame 80 read, closing a gap this row had left.** *It had been skipped in the original sweep and the omission only surfaced when the page ranges were written up for [Record Atlas](/method/). **Carta 37, June–August 1778, four marriages, nil for the name.** The range is now contiguous, 79–85.* *(A page range you cannot state honestly is a page range you have not read.)*

«Vittorio Franceschi», 29 Apr 1782 — one of two men
Antonio: a possible son, and the bell-rope moving on
rows.got:
**Six frames, two findings, four nils named — and one lesson about indexes.**

| frame | carta | date | what |
|---|---|---|---|
| **86** | 43 | **11 Nov 1780** | **Gregorio Defranceschi q.m Ant.o**, witness, beside Gasparo Bratulich q.m Vitt.o campanaro |
| 87 | 44 | Nov 1780 – Jan 1781 | nil — witnesses Fabris, Bonich, Bratulich |

| 89 | 46 | Jul – Oct 1781 | nil |

| 91 | 48 | May – Dec 1782 | nil; the year closes «Fine dell'Anno 1782: Matrimonij 10» |

**⚠ The reading on frame 86 carries a caveat and it is printed with the finding.** *An ink blot removes the last letters of the surname and the abbreviation before «Ant.o». The mark that survives has the same shape as the undoubted «**q.m** Vitt.o» **on the next line, same ink, same pen** — which is the only comparison this archive accepts. **Given as doc for the name; the blot is stated.***

**⚠ Frame 90 is the methodological find.** *The archpriest changes from **D. Antonio Massalini** to **D. Paolo Cossaich**, and with him the spelling: «Franceschi», not «Defranceschi».* **A name-indexed search for this family would lose them at exactly this page** — *which is the argument for reading the film.*

**And the office moved.** *Five namings of the campanaro across 1780–82, all **Bratulich** (Gasparo q.m Vittorio; Zorzi q.m Vittorio). After twenty years of a Defranceschi at every wedding, the standing witnesses are now other families.* *(doc.)*

**The nils are not empty.** *Frame 91, **1 June 1782**: «Pellagio q.m Dio: Giacomo Colla **nato nel luoco di Muina nella Carnia**» marries «Orsola figlia di Domenico Verona **pura nativa in Carnia**», both now resident in the parish. **Muina is in Ovaro, Carnia.*** *Two more Carnians at the castle, a century after the settlement.*

rows.src: «Capo» Antonio, alive in 1783 — and a reading of my own withdrawn
rows.what: Svetvinčenat marriages, film 005497886 frames 92–93 (1783) — read frame by frame
ev: The Svetvinčenat line — frame 93 in the story
Eufemia Bergamo — an empty stub, now evidenced
rows.got:
**Two frames, two findings, and a correction to work published four hours earlier.**

| frame | carta | date | what |
|---|---|---|---|
| 92 | 49 | Jan – Mar 1783 | nil — a new campanaro appears, **Pietro Brunetti** |
| **93** | 50 | **13 Mar 1783** | **Vittorio figlio di Capo Antonio de Franceschi × Eufemia figlia di Mattio Bergamo**, at **Parenzo** |
| **93** | 50 | **28 Apr 1783** | **Capo Antonio de Franceschi**, witness |

**⚠ «Capo», not «quondam» — and that overturns this morning's reading of frame 86.**

*Frame 86 had been published as «Gregorio Defranceschi **q.m** Ant.o», of the **late** Antonio, from a glyph an ink blot sits on. **Two acts of 1783 show Antonio alive and titled**, and the same clerk marks his dead in the same sentences — «**deff.o** Antonio Gigante», «Mattio Percich **q.** Piero», «Capo Mattio Buzzalovich **q.** Zuanne» — so the control is inside the line.* **The reading is withdrawn. [The correction is on the record.](/corrections/)**

**The rule earned:** *the comparison was made against the right line and still got it wrong, because **the mark being compared was never fully visible**. Where ink covers the decisive letter, the honest reading is no reading.*

**«Capo» itself is recorded, not translated.** *[A second construction was required before reading it at all](/method/), and the same act supplies one: «**Capo** Mattio Buzzalovich q. Zuanne **da Lisignano**». **What the title meant at Svetvinčenat is not established** — head of a contrada, of a household, or master of a boat. That both this Capo's wedding is held **at Parenzo** and the other Capo comes from **Ližnjan** is suggestive and is not evidence.*

**What the marriage settles.** *It **names Vittorio's father in a document** for the first time. It gives **Eufemia** a maiden name and a father — **Bergamo** — where this archive held only an **empty stub imported from the family tree**, a name with no evidence behind it; reading the film put the act under it. And it explains the «**pariter**» of the September 1783 font: she carried the name by marriage.*

**⚠ And they married away from home.** *At **Parenzo**, in the church of the B.V. degli Angeli, dispensed from the three banns **and from the closed season** — it is Lent — with witnesses from Parenzo and Ližnjan and none from the castle. **The register gives the dispensation and not the reason.***

rows.src: The pier's own construction file — and my best candidate for it got weaker
rows.what: Hungaricana + the City of Rijeka's port history — who is the «De Francescijev gat» named for? (item 157)
ev: The pier, and the candidate demoted
Ferencz Defranceschi of the Fiume Maritime Authority
Where the pier lives until a document ties it to somebody
rows.got:
**Asked properly for the first time. The pier gained a construction file; the best candidate lost ground.**

**Nil, with the exact terms named** *(on Hungaricana, where Fiume's officials actually live)*:

| term | hits |
|---|---|
| `"Defranceschi" móló` | **0** |
| `"Defranceschi" gát` | **0** |
| `"molo Defranceschi"` | **0** |
| `"molo De Franceschi"` | **0** |
| `"De Franceschi" móló` | **0** |
| *control* `Defranceschi révkapitány` | **5** |
| *control* `Defranceschi kikötő` | **1** |

**The controls pass in the same minutes**, so the zeros are real. *But they are **weak** evidence: this portal records pensions and salaries, not quaysides.*

**What was gained.** *The City of Rijeka's own port history places the pier in a single building programme: «**nasipavanjem zapadne obale izgrađeno je Istarsko, Bečko, Budimpeštansko i Praško pristanište te De Francheschijev i Visinov gat**» — to the designs of **Antal Hajnal**, chief engineer of the Hungarian royal port office. **Four wharves named for places, two gats named for people.** Warehouse 17 on the Visinov gat dates the set in use: **1906–07, Ferenc Pfaff**. ⚠ **The page does not say who either man was.*** *(doc for the grouping.)*

**⚠ What was lost.** *The **Budapesti utasító of 1848** (p. 70) shows the **Fiume harbour captaincy held by «Kapitány Sgardelli Alajos»**, while **«Főnök Defranceschi Ferencz»** ran the **quarantine institute at Martinšćica**. His «révkapitány» title appears only at his 1857 pensioning, filed under «**Fiumei tengerészeti hatóság**» — **the authority for the whole Hungarian Littoral, not a posting**.*

**So «port captain of Fiume» is withdrawn as a description of him**, and the intuition that carried him as the pier's eponym — the port official on the spot when the port was built — is not available: **Hajnal's programme is decades after he retired.** *He is not eliminated. He is no longer the comfortable answer.* **(open.)**

*Still unrun: Državni arhiv u Rijeci, the city's quay-renaming decrees, the Italian-era port plans 1924–45. The Lučka uprava chronology returned **HTTP 520** today.*

rows.src: The port authority's own chronology names no pier of that era
rows.what: Lučka uprava Rijeka — «Luka kroz povijest», the full chronology 1717–2025 (item 157, retried)
ev: The pier, and what the chronology does and does not give
rows.got:
**Retried at David's word, and it is a nil — but a clean, exhausting one.**

*The page returns **HTTP 520** to a fetcher, twice. **It loads normally in a browser**, which is how it was read: the whole chronology, **1717 to 2025**, is on one page.*

**⚠ It names no pier of the Hungarian era at all.** *Searched the full text for `gat`, `pristani`, `Zichy`, `Franceschi`, `Francheschi`, `Hajnal`, `Visinov`, `molo`, `lukobran`, `obal`. **The first quay the chronology names is «Orlandov gat», in 2013.*** *So the port authority's own public history does not carry the pier's name, and this route is now **exhausted rather than untried**.*

**What it gives instead is a frame, and one date that matters.**

| year | verbatim |
|---|---|
| **1855** | *«Započinju prvi radovi na izgradnji suvremene riječke luke premještanjem ušća Rječine u novo korito»* |
| **1867** | *the great basin begun; «Rijeka postaje glavna postaja za izlaz mađarskog gospodarstva u svijet»* |
| **⚠ 1941–45** | *«Njemačka vojska je prilikom povlačenja iz riječke luke **porušila sve vezove za prihvat brodova**… i više od 50% skladišnih kapaciteta»* |

**1867 opens the frame Hajnal's programme sits in — ten years after [Ferencz](/rijeka/) had already retired**, which is consistent with this morning's demotion of him.

**⚠ And 1941–45 sharpens the naming question.** *Every berth in the port was destroyed on the German withdrawal, and reconstruction followed in 1950. **A port rebuilt from nothing is exactly when quays get renamed**, and «De Franceschi**jev**» is a Croatian possessive — the form a post-1945 naming would take.* **Against it**: *the City of Rijeka attributes the gat name to Hajnal's Hungarian-era programme.* **Both are doc; neither inference is drawn.** *(nil for the name; the dates are the gain.)*

rows.what: Svetvinčenat marriages, film 005497886 frames 94–96 (1783–1784) — read frame by frame
ev: The Svetvinčenat line — 1784 in the story
Zuanne, son of the late Giacomo, m. 19 July 1784
rows.got:
**Resumed after the sign-out. Three frames, two findings, and a pattern that can now be counted.**

| frame | carta | date | what |
|---|---|---|---|
| 94 | 51 | Jul–Nov 1783 | nil for the name — *but a Carnian: **Giacomo Puspil q. Mattio, «nato nella Villa di Prato in Carnia Diocesi di Udine»**, 9 Oct* |
| 95 | 52 | Nov 1783 – Feb 1784 | nil; **«Fine dell'Anno 1783: Matrimonij N.o 26»** |
| **96** | 53 | **21 Feb 1784** | **Gio: Batta Steffanutto, «nativo della Carnia», «vedovo della q. Antonia nata de Franceschi»**, remarries |
| **96** | 53 | **19 Jul 1784** | **Zuanne figlio del q. Giacomo de Franceschi** × Antonia, daughter of the late Antonio |

**Zuanne is the first son of Jacobo's household the marriage book has named.** *This line knew it only through its women.* **⚠ But he is not assigned a father**: *the castle's Giacomo is the one this archive files as «at least two men», and the act does not decide which — only that his father was a Giacomo de Franceschi of this parish, dead by 1784.*

**Antonia is dead, and named.** *«**nata de Franceschi**» settles what the 1779 act left to a patronymic. **Bracket 7 Jan 1779 × 21 Feb 1784**, at thirty-six or younger; no year printable. Third woman on this line whose death is known only from her widower's next wedding.*

**⚠ Open, and deliberately not resolved:** *the new bride is «Angiola relitta q. Domenico **Galluzzi**»; Antonia's mother Pascasia had remarried a **Calluzzi**. One letter in one hand. Recorded, not claimed.*

**The Carnian count, read forward off this film: five in ten years** — *Corva (1774), Stefanuto (1779, and again 1784), Colla × Verona (1782), Puspil (1783). Two name the diocese of Udine; two name the village — **Muina** and **Prato**, both in the upper Degano, a few miles apart.* **That the parish kept marrying along the Carnian road is doc. That the Defranceschi came down it is not proved by these acts and is not claimed.**

**Frame 97 read 29 September — nil.** *Carta 54, October 1784 to January 1785; **«Fine dell'Anno 1784: Matrimonij N.o 14»**. ⚠ Two of its acts are again celebrated away from the parish church — one at **Castel S. Lorenzo** by licence to that pievano, one in **the church of S. Rocco** — which is the [rule this film has now earned twice over](/method/).*
